umm-al-quwain/ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Cost follows the stage of the programme more than the subject, because what is being bought changes. These notes set out what families here typically spend their hours on at each stage.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The cheapest point in the whole journey to buy help, and the one families skip. Sessions here are shorter, the content is less specialised, and the market rate sits at the lower end because a strong generalist can teach it well. One term in Year 9 often costs less than a month of rescue work in the final Diploma year.
programmes.countryNote: In this emirate the saving is larger than average, because the alternative later is a scarce Higher Level specialist in a term when every slot is taken. Families in Al Raas and Al Riqqa who start at Middle Years Programme level typically spend less in total across five years than those who start in the second Diploma year.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, first year
programmes.description: The best value hours in the Diploma, because Internal Assessment marks are still available and the exploration or investigation is worth around a fifth of a subject grade. A block of sessions on a research question and a method, bought early, is cheaper than the same marks chased through paper practice a year later.
programmes.countryNote: The school's internal deadline list governs when this spend is useful, and students here attend schools in other emirates with their own draft dates. Buying Internal Assessment support two weeks before a school deadline costs the same as buying it two months before and delivers considerably less.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme, final year
programmes.description: The most expensive hours in the market, for two reasons. Specialists are scarcest in the months before a session, so the premium band applies, and the work itself is paper practice and marking, which is labour-intensive. Market rates for named specialist exam-year support run at the upper end of every published range.
programmes.countryNote: Families here feel this harder than most because the pool is small and the choice narrows first in the northern emirates. Arranging final-year support during the first term, rather than in the term the papers are sat, is the single largest saving available to a parent in this emirate.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects
programmes.description: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies run alongside the licensed curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations, and support for them is priced like any other subject. Because the use of different or additional content for these subjects requires prior Ministry permission, the work follows the school's own scheme.
programmes.countryNote: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so there is no emirate-level fee or curriculum framework to compare against. Ask the school directly what is required before paying for support in these subjects.

umm-al-quwain/ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Some subjects carry a premium and others do not, and it is scarcity rather than difficulty that sets it. These entries say which is which for families searching from this emirate.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested subject in the market, so supply is reasonable and rates sit mid-band at Standard Level. Higher Level, particularly the third paper, is where the premium appears, because the pool of tutors who have taught sustained problem-solving to examination standard is much smaller than the pool who can teach the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Priced similarly to Analysis and Approaches, with one difference worth knowing: the course rewards calculator technique, so an hour spent on keystrokes and reasoning returns marks quickly. That makes short blocks unusually cost-effective compared with an open-ended weekly commitment.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The most common Higher Level request from this emirate and one of the clearest premium subjects. Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms need a genuine specialist, and in a small emirate there is rarely one within driving distance at any rate, which is why the local search returns so little.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: A premium subject for the same reason, with the added point that much of the available improvement is in method habits - symbols before numbers, units carried through - which are cheap to fix once diagnosed. A short diagnostic block often costs less and returns more than a term of weekly sessions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Mid-band pricing with good availability. Because the losses are usually terminology precision and command-term mismatch rather than conceptual gaps, families often buy fewer hours here than they expect to and spend them on spoken recall testing rather than on content delivery.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Widely available and mid-band, with essay marking the labour-intensive part. Pricing conversations here should be about how much written work is marked per month rather than about the hourly figure, because marking is where the cost and the value both sit.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: Reasonable availability at mid-band rates. The Internal Assessment work - commentaries within strict word limits, or a case-based report - is the part worth buying early, since those marks are banked once submitted and cannot be recovered through paper practice later.

subjects.name: Group 2 languages and specialist options
subjects.description: The genuine scarcity cases. A less commonly taught second language or a specialist Higher Level option paper may have no local tutor in the northern emirates at all, which is why those requests take longest to match and why a non-local specialist is sometimes the only real option.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Usually bought as a short block rather than weekly, and priced accordingly. The work is criteria reading and interrogation of a draft the student has written, so three or four well-timed sessions around the school's draft dates typically do more than a standing commitment.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Priced like any language subject, with the constraint that support follows the school's own scheme because additional content for these mandatory subjects requires prior Ministry permission. Ask what the school expects before committing to a block.

sections.heading: What a local search actually returns in Umm Al Quwain
paragraphs: Type the query and look at what comes back. A handful of directory listings, most of them for Dubai businesses with a national service area. Some centre-based providers in Sharjah or Ajman. A few classified adverts. Almost no prices, and almost nothing that names a subject at a level - which is the only thing that matters for an IB student.

The reason is structural rather than suspicious. Local search ranks businesses by proximity, prominence and relevance, and a small emirate with few registered tutoring businesses has little to rank. The listings that do appear are frequently serving the whole country from elsewhere, which means the map pin is telling you where a company registered, not where a tutor sits.

This produces a specific risk for a parent. The nearest listing looks like the lowest-friction option, so it gets the call, and the conversation starts with availability rather than with whether anybody there has taught Higher Level Chemistry. A quote arrives, it sounds reasonable, and nobody has yet asked what the tutor will actually be marking. That is how a family ends up paying mid-band rates for a generalist.

The better sequence inverts it. Decide the subject, level and the examination session first. Ask what is set and marked between sessions. Ask the rate, in dirhams, per hour, with what is included. Only then consider where anybody is sitting - and for a format delivered over live video, that last question stops mattering at all.

sections.heading: The price of an hour, and the six things that move it
paragraphs: Two quotes for the same subject can differ by more than AED 200 an hour, and quality explains less of that gap than parents assume. Six factors do most of the work, and they are all askable about on a first call.

Level comes first: Higher Level commands more than Standard Level because the teaching pool is smaller, and the gap widens for papers few tutors have taught. Scarcity is second and is partly about the subject - a specialist option paper or a less commonly taught language has no local supply in the northern emirates - and partly about the hour: a 6pm Gulf Standard Time slot on a weekday is the most contested hour in the week. Format is third, and it is where the biggest single difference sits, because an in-home visit prices the travel as well as the teaching.

Session length is fourth and is often mispriced in a family's favour. Ninety minutes rarely costs 50% more than sixty in the market, but it does not produce 50% more learning for a tired student after a long commute, so the cheaper unit rate can be false economy. Proximity to the examination session is fifth: specialist availability tightens in the final two terms and the premium bands apply. Travel is sixth, and in this emirate it is the loudest of the six.

What should not move a price is a promise about outcomes. A rate justified by a claimed grade improvement is being justified by something nobody can evidence or deliver, and in a market where one provider sells completed Internal Assessments outright, a premium attached to a result rather than to a service deserves scepticism.

sections.heading: Market rates in dirhams, with sources
paragraphs: Here are the bands, compiled from providers' own published figures and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table, with the source named beside each so a parent can judge rather than trust. The figures below describe the market; they are not IB Gram's price list.

At the entry level, online tuition from a university student or a general tutor is advertised from the mid-forties upward in dirhams per hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online occupies the band most families here end up in, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. For an in-home visit with travel included, Bestimate shows AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. A named IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist runs from around AED 200 to AED 450 and beyond, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. At the top, premium examiner-marketed tutors reach AED 500 to 650 or more, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Packages are quoted monthly as often as hourly. The market shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Two cautions before comparing. First, check what the monthly figure includes: eight sessions a month at AED 799 is a different product from four if marking is included in one and not the other. Second, a rate quoted in dollars or pounds by an international platform usually lands at the upper end of the dirham band once converted, which is worth doing before a comparison rather than after a payment.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, entries and the two-year plan
paragraphs: An hourly rate means nothing without a total, and a total means nothing without the rest of the education budget beside it. This is the calculation almost no tutoring page shows, and it is the one that actually decides how many hours a family buys.

Start with the fee environment. Dubai's authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under the second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Dubai also added seven new private schools for 2026-27, four British curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places after a 6% enrolment rise in 2025-26. That is a Dubai picture, not a northern-emirates one, but it sets the backdrop: fees are the dominant line and tutoring is the discretionary one.

Then build the tutoring total for a realistic plan rather than a worst case. One subject at one weekly hour through a school year is around 30 to 34 sessions. Two subjects in the final year, plus a block for each Internal Assessment and a short intensive before the session, is the heaviest pattern most families here run, and it is worth costing out on paper before the first session rather than discovering it in April.

Private candidate entry fees are a separate line and are set by the school or centre entering the student, not by a tutor. If a student is being entered privately rather than through a school, ask the centre for the fee in writing early, because it varies by centre and series and it is not something any tutoring service can quote for you.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, without naming a villain
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market compares itself against an unnamed straw man. A more useful comparison is between models, because each has a genuine case and a genuine weakness, and a family's circumstances decide which fits.

A specialist agency matches by subject and usually marks work, at a mid to upper rate. An international marketplace offers the widest choice and the least quality control, often quoting in another currency. A freelance independent tutor can be excellent and is the only model where a parent deals directly with the teacher, but there is no replacement if the match fails and no second opinion if it drifts. A tuition centre group class is the cheapest per hour and the least individual, which suits content revision and not a specific criterion problem. School-run support is usually free and tied to the teacher who already teaches the class.

Across all of them, two questions separate a good arrangement from a bad one at any price. What is set and marked between sessions? And what happens if the match is wrong? A model that cannot answer the second is asking a family to carry the risk of its matching, which matters more in a small emirate where the alternative pool is thin.

One legal check applies to every model. Paid private tutoring in the UAE runs through a work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so any amount quoted online is unverified. Since the permit costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one has simply not done it, and that is a fair thing to ask about before paying anybody.

sections.heading: What a cheap hour usually costs later
paragraphs: The budget band is real and it has legitimate uses. For Middle Years Programme homework support, for building recall in a content-heavy subject, or for a student who mainly needs company and structure while working, a tutor at the lower end of the market is good value and nobody should be talked out of it.

Where it goes wrong is the Diploma. The marks a Diploma student is losing are usually technical: a command term read at the wrong depth, an Internal Assessment criterion misunderstood, method marks not claimed because working was not shown. Diagnosing those requires somebody who has used the mark scheme, and that is exactly what the lower band does not buy. The hour is pleasant, the student feels helped, and the same three errors appear on the next script.

The cost shows up twice. Once in the fee for hours that produced no diagnosis, and again in the lost time, which is the expensive part. A term spent on the wrong problem in the first Diploma year is a term unavailable later, and in this emirate the later term is when specialist availability is tightest and the premium band applies. The cheap hour is frequently the most expensive purchase in the plan.

The practical defence is not to spend more. It is to spend the first hour on a diagnostic and demand a written output from it: the specific marks being lost, named, with the command terms or criteria involved. That costs nothing when the trial session is free, and it tells you in an hour what six weeks of pleasant sessions will not.

sections.heading: VAT, cancellations and the questions nobody asks before paying
paragraphs: Most of the unpleasant surprises in tutoring are administrative rather than academic, and all of them are avoidable with four questions asked before the first payment.

First, is the quoted figure per hour or per session? A ninety-minute session quoted at an hourly rate is a different number from the one a parent heard, and this is the most common misunderstanding in the market. Second, is the quoted price inclusive of VAT? The correct answer is a clear statement about the specific price being quoted; the UAE tax treatment of education services is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority and not something a tutoring page should characterise, so ask the provider to state plainly whether their own figure includes it.

Third, what is the cancellation and rescheduling policy, in hours? A student in this emirate can be delayed by a school bus, and a policy requiring twenty-four hours' notice behaves very differently from one requiring twelve. Ask also what happens if the tutor cancels, which providers mention less often. Fourth, what exactly is included: is marking of set work inside the hourly rate or billed separately, and how many pieces per month?

A fifth question is worth adding wherever the word free appears. A free trial should come with its stated conditions visible on the same screen - how long it lasts, who it is available to, and whether any card details are required. Ours is one session with the tutor who would teach, with no card required and no obligation. Any version of that offer worth taking will answer the same three points without being chased.

sections.heading: What proximity costs you in choice
paragraphs: Return to the original search. A parent looking for a tutor near them in Umm Al Quwain is applying a filter that, in this emirate, removes most of the useful options before the conversation starts. It is worth being precise about what is being traded.

What proximity buys is real: a person in the room, physical materials, supervision of a younger child, and for some students a level of engagement a screen does not produce. For a Middle Years Programme student who will not work with a laptop, that is decisive and a family should act on it.

What it costs is choice and reliability. The pool within driving distance of this emirate is small, and the subset of it that has taught a given Higher Level course to examination standard is smaller again, often empty. Once a tutor has to drive an hour each way, the arrangement carries a loading in the rate, a minimum booking, or a fragile slot - and in the final Diploma year, a fragile slot is the costly failure, because the weeks lost cannot be bought back at any price.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and no UAE office or centre exists. The trade on offer here is explicit: no travel charge, a specialist matched to the course rather than the postcode, a fixed slot in Gulf Standard Time, and a free trial lesson so the match is tested before any money moves. For a family in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Humrah, that is usually not a compromise but the only version of the service that works.

faqs.question: How much does an IB tutor cost per hour for a family in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Market rates, with sources, run roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit including travel, and AED 200 to 450 or more for a named IB specialist, with premium examiner-marketed tutors at AED 500 to 650 and above. Most families in this emirate end up in the qualified-subject-tutor band. Those are market figures compiled from providers' own published rates and Bestimate's 2026 table, not IB Gram's price list, and our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Why does an in-home quote here cost more than the same quote in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Because of the drive. The nearest concentration of IB subject teachers sits around the Sharjah and Ajman schools, roughly an hour from most of Umm Al Quwain in ordinary traffic, so a one-hour booking costs the tutor two hours of travel. That gets paid for in one of three ways: a higher hourly rate, a two-hour minimum booking, or a slot that moves whenever the road does. Published in-home bands of AED 180 to 500 are Dubai-market figures, and quotes from this emirate tend to sit at or above the top of them.

faqs.question: What makes one tutor's rate AED 150 and another's AED 400?
faqs.answer: Six things, and quality is only part of one of them. Higher Level costs more than Standard Level because the pool is smaller. A scarce subject or a specialist option paper costs more, or has no local supply at all. An in-home format prices travel as well as teaching. A longer session has a lower unit rate. Rates rise in the final two terms before an examination session as availability tightens. And distance to this emirate loads the number. Ask about each and most of the gap between two quotes explains itself.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying per hour?
faqs.answer: Only if you check what is in it. The market shows around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, but eight sessions with marking included is a different product from eight without. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Compare the per-session figure, then compare what is marked, before comparing the headline monthly number.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time to buy IB tutoring?
faqs.answer: Early, and this is the largest saving available to a family in this emirate. Internal Assessment marks are worth around a fifth of a subject grade, are available in the first Diploma year, and are banked once submitted - so a block bought around the school's draft dates costs the same as one bought late and delivers considerably more. In the final two terms, specialist availability is tightest, premium bands apply and the choice narrows first in the northern emirates. The expensive route is discovering in the final term that you need somebody scarce.

faqs.question: Does a tutoring price quoted to an Umm Al Quwain family include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask the provider to state it plainly about their own figure, and get the answer in writing. The UAE tax treatment of education services is a matter for the Federal Tax Authority, and a tutoring page should not characterise it; what a parent needs is a clear statement about the specific number being quoted to them. While you are asking, settle the other three administrative questions too: whether the rate is per hour or per session, how many marked pieces a month are included, and the cancellation window in hours in both directions.

faqs.question: What should the cancellation policy be for a student commuting from this emirate?
faqs.answer: Shorter notice than a Dubai policy would need, because a school bus from Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah can be delayed by an hour without warning. A twelve-hour window behaves very differently from a twenty-four-hour one in practice. Ask the question in both directions: what happens if your child cannot make the slot, and what happens if the tutor cancels. The second is mentioned far less often in this market and is the one that costs a family a week of planned revision.

faqs.question: Is a group class cheaper and is it worth it?
faqs.answer: Cheaper per hour, yes, and worth it for some purposes. Group classes suit content revision, recall practice and structure, and for a student who simply needs to cover ground again they are good value. They do not suit the thing most Diploma students are actually losing marks to, which is specific: one criterion misread, one command term answered at the wrong depth, method marks not claimed. Diagnosing that requires somebody looking at your child's own script, which a group format does not provide at any price.

faqs.question: Do you charge for the trial lesson or ask for card details?
faqs.answer: No. The trial is one session with the tutor who would actually teach, with no card required and no obligation to continue, and it produces a written diagnostic you keep whether or not you proceed. That document names the specific marks being lost and the command terms or criteria involved. Wherever you see the word free in this market, ask for the conditions on the same screen: how long the trial is, who it is open to, and whether any payment details are needed up front.

faqs.question: Can we pay for a fixed block rather than committing weekly?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some purposes a block is the better purchase. Three to six sessions aimed at one Internal Assessment, one oral or one paper gives a family a known total and no standing commitment, and it is often the highest-value spend in the Diploma because those marks are banked once the work is submitted. Weekly sessions earn their keep differently: the diagnosis improves with each marked script and the error log carries forward, which is why a term or more is where the weekly format pays.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor is legally allowed to take payment in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the private tutor work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so any figure quoted to you is unverified - and since the permit is free, not having one is a choice.

faqs.question: How many hours in total should we budget for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Cost the realistic pattern rather than the worst case. One subject at one weekly hour through a school year is about 30 to 34 sessions. The heaviest arrangement most families here run is two subjects weekly in the final year, plus a block for each Internal Assessment and a short intensive before the session. Put that on paper before the first session rather than discovering it in April. And remember the alternative to planning it is not spending less - it is spending more, later, when availability is tightest.

faqs.question: Are international platforms quoting in dollars cheaper than local rates?
faqs.answer: Usually not, once converted. Two of the pages ranking for these queries quote in US dollars and one leads with pounds, and the resulting figures generally land at the upper end of the dirham band. The conversion takes two minutes and is worth doing before a comparison rather than after a payment. There is a second thing to check with an overseas platform: whether the conversion path for support and scheduling runs through a UAE contact point, and whether the quoted rate includes the marking a Diploma student needs.

faqs.question: Should we pay more for a tutor who advertises examiner experience?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and even then for a specific reason. Current examiner status is not something a family can easily verify, and it should never be presented as access to marking, boundaries or paper content, because no such access exists. What a genuinely experienced marker offers is scheme literacy - method marks, error carried forward, level descriptors - and that is testable in a trial session by watching how they mark a piece of your child's work. Test the marking rather than the title, and let the premium follow what you see.

intro.heading: What a family here is actually buying when they ask for a home tutor
paragraphs: The phrase home tutor describes a delivery method, and most parents who type it are describing something else: a child who has fallen behind in two subjects, an exam series that is closer than it looks, and no realistic way to drive anywhere after a school run that ends at five. The home visit is the solution they have seen advertised. It is not necessarily the solution that fits Umm Al Quwain.

Start with the arithmetic that nobody itemises. A specialist who teaches Cambridge Chemistry 0620 or Pearson Edexcel Mathematics A 4MA1 is far more likely to be based in Dubai or Sharjah than in this emirate. A round trip to Al Salamah or Al Raas costs that tutor between ninety minutes and two hours of unpaid time on a weekday evening. Market quotes reflect it: UAE in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching online, with Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table putting in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and home tutor listings reaching AED 500.

Then look at what the premium buys. It does not buy a better teacher, because the same person charges both rates. It buys their presence, and the price of that presence is paid twice: once in dirhams, and once in the size of the pool you can choose from. The tutors willing to drive to Falaj Al Mualla on a Tuesday evening are a small subset of the tutors who can teach Additional Mathematics 0606, and the overlap between those two sets is where most northern-emirates families get stuck.

The useful question is therefore not whether a tutor sits beside your child, but which parts of an IGCSE actually require it. That turns out to be a short and specific list, and this page works through it component by component: written papers, practical science, the alternative-to-practical paper, speaking components, coursework and timed paper practice. Some of those benefit from presence. Most do not, and two are taught better on a screen because the mark scheme and the student's own written work can both be visible at once.

IB Gram delivers tuition for UAE families as one-to-one live video lessons. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and no tutor is sent to an address in Umm Al Quwain. What a family here gets instead is a specialist in the exact specification their child is entered for, a fixed weekly slot that survives a long commute, and written feedback after every session that can be read against the school's own reports. The rest of this page is the working behind that position rather than the assertion of it.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programme stages and one administrative reality shape what a tutor can do for a student in this emirate. The notes below are specific to Umm Al Quwain rather than to the UAE in general.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Separate syllabuses with separate codes, most of them tiered Core or Extended. Sciences add either a practical test sat at the centre or a written alternative-to-practical paper. The examined components, not the textbook, decide what a weekly hour should contain in the two years before the series.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students are usually entered through a centre in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, because the school is there. Practical tests therefore happen in another emirate on a date set by that centre, which is one reason a visiting tutor cannot help with that component wherever they live.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Mathematics A 4MA1 is tiered Foundation or Higher; the separate sciences 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 are single-tier and examine practical skills inside the written papers. Grades are reported 9 to 1. Exams run in May/June and November, so a resit in a single subject is a genuine planning option.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. For a northern-emirates student who missed a grade in June, that November window is close enough to work towards without losing a year.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects alongside the international programme
programmes.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies run beside the licensed international curriculum in UAE private schools. They are examined and reported by the school, and they are frequently the subjects a family discovers late, because the IGCSE conversation at home is about maths and science.
programmes.countryNote: KHDA's guidance for Dubai schools requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and prohibits combined classes because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Schools in Umm Al Quwain sit under Ministry of Education supervision, so confirm the stream your child is placed in with the school.

programmes.name: The grades that open Year 12
programmes.description: IGCSE results are entry conditions. Schools typically want a grade 6 or a B before an A Level subject and a 7 or an A before a Higher Level Diploma subject. Maths and the sciences are the common blockers, which is why a grade 5 in Year 11 narrows choices two years before anyone applies anywhere.
programmes.countryNote: For the Ministry of Education's British track, equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. Check the current requirement on moe.gov.ae before planning around it.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by what a weekly hour actually repairs in it, and by whether any part of it genuinely needs an adult physically present. That is the decision this page exists to help with.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: A weekly hour repairs unwritten working, non-calculator fluency and the identification move on multi-step questions. Nothing in it needs presence: a shared screen with the student's photographed working and the mark scheme side by side shows more than a tutor leaning over a kitchen table can.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The repairs are formula selection, unit handling and the apparatus questions on the alternative-to-practical paper. The one component that needs a room is the Cambridge practical test, and that is sat at the exam centre under supervision where no private tutor may be present anyway.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Mole and reacting-mass calculations are the grade, and they are repaired by making the sequence of steps fixed and written. Qualitative analysis is recall of a table. Both are screen-friendly; the lab work belongs to the school and stays there.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Volume of content is the problem. The weekly repair is converting general description into named structures, named processes and stated directions of movement, which means rewriting the student's own answers against the mark scheme rather than re-reading notes.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Summary content points and matching register to a stated audience are the two repairs that move a grade. Annotating the student's own writing live on a shared screen is the core activity, and it is one of the few things that works better remotely than over a printed page.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: The speaking component is where families assume presence is needed. It is not: the test is a conversation with an examiner, and preparing for it over video with a microphone is closer to the real conditions than practising across a sofa.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Application to the named case business and a judgement at the end of extended answers. The repair is structural: planning an answer in thirty seconds before writing. Shared documents make that visible in a way a paper notebook does not.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and logic gates. Screen sharing is the native environment for this subject, and a tutor who can watch a student's code execute line by line is better placed than one reading over their shoulder.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Calculus and trigonometric identities a year early. Specialists are scarce across the northern emirates, so this is the clearest case where insisting on a visiting tutor means not getting the subject taught at all.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Taught beside the international curriculum under UAE rules, with different expectations for Arab and non-Arab students. A tutor must know which stream the school has placed the student in, because the two are marked against different expectations.

sections.heading: In-home against one-to-one online, for this emirate specifically
paragraphs: The comparison most providers publish is written to make one option look foolish. The honest version has losses on both sides. A visiting tutor can read body language across a table, can confiscate a phone, and can sit with a reluctant fourteen-year-old in a way that is harder through a screen. Those are real advantages and parents of younger or easily distracted students should weigh them seriously.

What a visit costs is also real. The market premium is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour depending on tier and distance, the pool of tutors shrinks to those who will drive to Umm Al Quwain on a school night, and a cancelled session cannot be recovered the same evening. For a family in Falaj Al Mualla the choice is frequently between a generalist who will travel and a specialist who will not.

The online version wins on three specific things rather than in general. It wins on tutor pool, because the match is made on the syllabus code. It wins on recovery, because a session missed on Tuesday can run on Wednesday without anybody rearranging a car. And it wins on evidence, because every annotated paper, mark-scheme comparison and written note exists as a file a parent can read rather than as a conversation at the front door.

sections.heading: Component by component: what actually needs a person in the room
paragraphs: An IGCSE is assessed through a small set of defined components, and the home-tutor question is best answered by going through them rather than by arguing about formats in the abstract. Written theory papers are the bulk of every subject, and they are prepared by doing questions and having them marked. Nothing about that requires physical presence; it requires the student's working and the mark scheme to be visible to both people at the same time, which is a screen-sharing problem.

Practical science at Cambridge splits in two. Where a centre enters candidates for the practical test, that test is sat at the centre under exam supervision, and no private tutor may be present whatever their location. Where the alternative-to-practical paper is sat instead, the component is entirely written: apparatus diagrams, variables, repeat readings, graph work and method criticism. It is one of the most predictable sources of marks on the specification and it is fully teachable over video from the board's own past papers.

Speaking components surprise people. A Cambridge English as a Second Language speaking test is a recorded conversation with an examiner, and rehearsing it over a microphone and a camera is closer to the real conditions than practising face to face in a living room. Coursework, where a centre has chosen that route, is the student's own work by rule, so the tutor's job there is criteria teaching and feedback on a draft, never production.

That leaves the genuine case for presence, which is behavioural rather than academic: a young student who will not stay in the chair, or one with a specific need for an adult physically beside them. Families in that position should say so in the enquiry. It is better to be told honestly that video teaching is a poor fit than to pay for three months of it and find out.

sections.heading: What the northern-emirates market charges, and where the number comes from
paragraphs: Rates in this part of the UAE are quoted privately, which makes it hard for a family to know whether a number is reasonable. The published bands are worth knowing before any conversation. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52, both online and generally with less experienced tutors. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes around AED 270 for specialist tutoring, and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table runs from AED 200 to 450 and above for exam-year specialists. At the top, BartyED has published AED 650.

In-home visits sit differently. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home-tutor listings reach AED 500. Monthly packages circulating in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those figures belong to the providers who published them, with the dates as stated.

What moves a quote in Umm Al Quwain specifically is distance, subject scarcity and the time of year. A Dubai-based chemistry specialist asked to drive to Al Raas prices the drive. A request for Additional Mathematics 0606 prices scarcity. A request made in March for the June series prices urgency, because the tutor is turning other work away. None of that is unreasonable, and all of it is avoidable information to have before you negotiate.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, and any page that quotes a figure as ours is wrong. The free trial lesson comes first, and pricing is discussed in the consultation that follows it, once somebody has actually seen the student work.

sections.heading: The student's own handwriting, and how it gets marked remotely
paragraphs: The objection parents raise most often is practical: IGCSE maths and chemistry are written subjects, so how does a tutor see the working? The answer has two parts and both matter more than the technology does. The student writes on paper, exactly as they will in the exam hall, because typing changes how mathematics is set out and how errors appear. A phone camera or a cheap document camera puts that paper on the shared screen.

What then happens is the part that an in-home session often skips. The tutor annotates the student's own page against the mark scheme, in front of them, marking where each method mark was earned and where one was available and unclaimed. The annotated page is saved and sent. Four weeks of those pages is a record of exactly which habits have changed, which is a different thing from a tutor's impression that things are going well.

For a timed paper the sequence is deliberately split across two sessions. The student sits the paper alone, to time, on a weekend morning, and photographs it. The tutor marks it before the next session, so the hour is spent entirely on the questions that lost marks rather than on watching a child write. Paying a visiting tutor to sit in a room while a student completes a two-hour paper is the single most expensive thing a family can do with a tutoring budget.
The one piece of equipment worth buying is a stand that holds a phone above the desk. Everything else - a laptop, a notebook, the subject's own textbook and a quiet corner - is already in the house.

sections.heading: Where local knowledge genuinely helps, and where it is irrelevant
paragraphs: Some things about a tutor's location do matter, and it is worth separating them from the things that do not. Knowing which exam centre a student is entered through matters, because the centre sets the timetable, the zone and the practical test date. Knowing the school's teaching order matters, because tutoring that runs three topics ahead of the class helps nobody. Knowing the school's internal assessment calendar matters, because that is when a student's workload spikes.

None of those require the tutor to live nearby. They require the tutor to ask, and to be told. A specialist in Dubai who has the centre's zone, the scheme of work and the date of the school's mock fortnight is better informed about your child's year than a neighbour who teaches without asking any of it.

Where living in the region does help is in the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies run alongside the international curriculum in UAE private schools, with different expectations for Arab and non-Arab students, and the language of instruction differs by stream. A tutor who has taught inside the UAE system understands why a child who speaks Arabic at home is struggling with first-language Arabic, which is a curriculum problem rather than a language one.

The irrelevant part is proximity itself. There is no pedagogical content in a tutor being fifteen minutes away rather than fifty, once the teaching is not happening in the room. What proximity buys is the possibility of a visit, which costs the premium set out above and narrows the choice to whoever is willing to drive.

sections.heading: How long each repair takes, and what counts as evidence it worked
paragraphs: Families here reasonably want to know how many sessions something takes. The honest answer varies by what is broken, and most of the common faults at IGCSE are habits with fairly predictable timelines. Unwritten working takes about four weeks of insistence to become automatic. Non-calculator fluency takes six to eight weeks of short weekly drills. Command-word technique shows up within three or four sessions, because it is a reading skill rather than a content gap.

Content gaps behave differently. A missing unit of work - electricity in physics, moles in chemistry, the genetics crosses in biology - takes two to four sessions to teach and then needs spaced revisiting, because teaching it once and moving on is how it got lost the first time. A student who is behind across a whole year is a different proposition and should be told so plainly rather than sold a weekly hour.

Evidence is the part parents should insist on. After four to six weeks there should be a comparable pair of marked questions: one from the first fortnight and one from the sixth week, on the same topic, marked the same way. If the second is not better, the plan is wrong, the tutor is wrong, or the diagnosis was wrong. Any of those is worth knowing in week six rather than in May.

The table sets out the common faults with the timeline each usually needs and the specific evidence that it has actually changed. Individual students vary and no tutor can promise a grade, but the shape of the repair is stable enough to plan around.

sections.heading: Two children, one household, two different boards
paragraphs: This is more common in the northern emirates than anywhere else in the country, because families change schools when the commute, the fee or a bus route changes, and the new school often uses a different board. A household in Al Raas can easily have one child on Cambridge 0580 maths and another on Pearson 4MA1, with different grade scales, different paper structures and different revision needs.

A single visiting tutor is a poor fit for that household, because few individuals teach both specifications well and the visit has to be shared or doubled. Over video the problem disappears: two different specialists take two different slots on two different evenings, each matched to the specification their student is actually sitting.

What families should not do is put two children in the same session to halve the cost. One-to-one works because the whole hour is diagnostic. Two students at different stages in the same hour produces something closer to a small class, and the quieter child reliably gets less. Where budget is the constraint, alternating weeks between children is a better compromise than sharing an hour.

The exception is two students in the same year, on the same specification, at the same tier, with similar current marks. That can work as a deliberate pair, and should be priced and planned as a pair rather than quietly arranged. Agreed in advance, a pair also makes marking comparisons useful, because both students sit the same paper to the same time and the two scripts can be read against each other.

One further household case is worth naming. Where an older sibling has already sat the series and a younger one is two years behind, the family tends to assume the same plan applies. Boards change specifications, tier decisions differ by school set, and the older child's past papers may no longer match the current syllabus. Check the codes again rather than inheriting them.

sections.heading: Who is in the room, what is recorded, and what we keep
paragraphs: A video lesson with a minor raises questions a visiting tutor raises differently, and they deserve a direct answer. Sessions take place in a shared household space wherever possible rather than behind a closed bedroom door, and a parent is welcome to sit in at any time without notice. That is a reasonable standard whatever the format, and families should apply it to in-home arrangements too.

On records, what exists after a session is the annotated work and a short written note of what was covered, marked and set. Lesson recordings are made only where a family asks for them and are shared with that family. A tutor does not publish or circulate a student's work.

On data, the enquiry asks for what is needed to make a match: year group, subjects, board, tier and the school's teaching position. There is no reason for a tutoring enquiry to collect a child's photograph, their full report card or their examination candidate number, and families should be wary of any form that asks. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs this, and a privacy link sits on every page of this site.

On permits, any individual providing private tuition in the UAE needs the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation and granted free of charge for two years. It is a fair question to ask any tutor, visiting or remote, and a straight answer is the minimum you should accept.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our house in Umm Al Quwain for IGCSE lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service offered only in India. The honest reason is worth knowing: the specialists who teach particular IGCSE specifications are mostly based in Dubai and Sharjah, and a round trip to this emirate costs them up to two hours of unpaid time on a school night. Families who insist on a visit are choosing from whoever will make that drive, rather than from whoever teaches the syllabus their child is actually entered for.

faqs.question: What does a visiting IGCSE tutor charge in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Published market figures put in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table gives AED 180 to 350, and independent home-tutor listings reach AED 500. Monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799. Online one-to-one with a qualified subject tutor is published lower, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are the providers' own figures as at October 2026, not IB Gram prices, and distance from Dubai pushes the in-home end upwards.

faqs.question: Which parts of an IGCSE genuinely need somebody sitting next to my child?
faqs.answer: Very few. Written theory papers, the alternative-to-practical paper, coursework feedback, speaking preparation and timed paper practice are all taught at least as well over video, because the student's work and the mark scheme can be on screen together. The Cambridge practical test is sat at the exam centre under supervision, where no private tutor may be present regardless of where they live. The genuine case for presence is behavioural rather than academic: a young or very distractible student who needs an adult physically beside them.

faqs.question: If my son writes on paper, what does the tutor actually see?
faqs.answer: He writes on paper exactly as he will in the exam hall, and a phone on a stand above the desk puts the page on the shared screen. The tutor then annotates that page against the published mark scheme while he watches, marking where method marks were earned and where one was available and missed. The annotated page is saved and sent afterwards. A stack of those pages over six weeks is a clearer record of what has changed than any verbal report at a front door.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor at AED 50 an hour a false economy at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Often, and the reason is specific rather than snobbish. Budget rates in this market, advertised from around AED 33 to 65 an hour, usually mean a tutor who knows the subject but not the specification: they will teach chemistry competently and not know that Paper 6 asks about variables and method criticism, or that Pearson examines practical skills inside the written papers. For content catch-up in Year 9 or early Year 10 that can be perfectly adequate. For an exam-year candidate at Extended or Higher tier, the specification knowledge is the thing you are paying for.

faqs.question: Can both of my children share one weekly session to halve the cost?
faqs.answer: It works only in a narrow case: same year, same specification, same tier, similar current marks, and planned as a pair from the start. Otherwise the hour stops being diagnostic and becomes a small class, and the quieter child reliably gets less of it. Where budget is the binding constraint, alternating weeks between two children usually produces more than splitting every hour between them. Households in this emirate quite often run two different boards across siblings, and in that case two separate specialists on two evenings is the cleaner answer.

faqs.question: Does it matter that the tutor has never visited my child's school?
faqs.answer: What matters is whether they ask for three things: the exam centre and its timetable zone, the school's scheme of work, and the date of the school's own mock fortnight. A specialist in Dubai who has all three is better informed about your child's year than a neighbour who teaches without asking for any of it. Proximity has no teaching content once the lesson is not happening in the room. It buys the possibility of a visit, at the market premium, from a smaller pool of tutors.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to fix working that is never written down?
faqs.answer: About four weeks of weekly insistence, in most cases. It is a habit rather than a knowledge gap: the student reaches a correct intermediate value mentally, writes only the final answer, slips on the arithmetic and collects nothing for work worth two or three marks. The repair is making the writing non-negotiable in every session and showing the student, on their own marked page, exactly how many marks the habit has been costing. It is the cheapest grade movement available at IGCSE and no new content is involved.

faqs.question: What is the earliest a session can realistically start in this emirate?
faqs.answer: Around 6pm on weekdays for most of Umm Al Quwain, and closer to 6.45pm or 7pm for families at the Marina, the corniche or Falaj Al Mualla. Students here commute to schools in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah and arrive home between 4.15pm and 5.15pm depending on the route. Anything taught after about 8.30pm is poorly retained. Weekend mornings are the only reliable window for a continuous ninety minutes, which is what a full timed paper needs.

faqs.question: Do lessons stop during Ramadan, or move?
faqs.answer: They move. School days shorten, the family rhythm changes, and most households here prefer a post-Iftar slot to a late-afternoon one. Pausing for a month in Year 11 is expensive in a way that rescheduling is not, particularly if a June series is the target, so the usual arrangement is to keep the weekly commitment and shift the hour later. Shorter, more frequent sessions also work well in that month for students who find a full hour heavy while fasting.

faqs.question: Can a tutor mark my daughter's IGCSE coursework draft for her?
faqs.answer: A tutor can read a draft she has written, explain the published criteria, say which criterion the draft is not meeting and teach the technique she then applies herself. A tutor cannot write, rewrite or substantially edit it. Coursework is submitted as the student's own work and board malpractice procedures fall on the candidate, so the cost of crossing that line is hers rather than the tutor's. Any provider offering to produce or complete assessed work is offering your daughter a risk she should not be taking.

faqs.question: Which details about my child should a tutoring enquiry not be asking for?
faqs.answer: A child's photograph, a full school report, a candidate number or a home address are not needed to match a tutor to a syllabus. What is legitimately needed is the year group, the subjects, the board, the tier and roughly where the student is. The UAE's Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection governs how a provider must handle a minor's data, and any form collecting more than it needs should state why and how to have it deleted. Ask before you fill it in.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor is allowed to take payment for lessons here?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, granted free of charge for two years, and the official route is the Private Tutor Licensing service on mohre.gov.ae, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 11 with mocks already behind him. Is a weekly hour enough?
faqs.answer: For one subject with a clear diagnosable fault, yes. For a student who is behind across the whole year in three subjects, no, and anybody who tells you otherwise is selling. The realistic structure from February onwards is two sessions a week in the priority subject - one to sit a paper to time and one to work through the losses - plus a decision about which subjects you are going to accept as they are. Choosing where not to spend is part of the plan, not a failure of it.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor you match us with is the wrong fit?
faqs.answer: Say so early, and the match is changed. The free trial exists partly for this: it is an hour of real teaching with a specialist, and most mismatches are visible in it. Where a problem emerges later - a personality clash, a pace that does not suit, a tutor whose strength turns out to be a different tier - the written session notes make the conversation concrete rather than awkward. A fit problem spotted in week three costs three hours; one ignored until March costs a term.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Decide on the format after the trial, not before it
umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: The home-tutor question is easier to answer once somebody has actually taught your child for an hour. Send the year group, the subjects, the board and the tier, and a specialist in that specification will run a free trial lesson with no charge and no card details. You will get a written diagnosis of what is weak and in what order to fix it, which is useful whichever way you then go. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed around the school run out of Umm Al Quwain, with the slot set in Gulf Standard Time. If video teaching is the wrong fit for your child, we will tell you that too.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raa.tutorsIntro: The profiles below cover the IGCSE subjects Al Raas families book most: Maths, the three separate sciences, English Language and Business Studies, across both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel specifications.

intro.heading: The search that matters is the board, not the neighbourhood
paragraphs: Parents in Al Raas usually start by drawing a circle. Who teaches IGCSE near the creek? Who would come from Al Riqqa, from Al Salamah, from UAQ Marina? The circle gets bigger, the list stays short, and after a week the family concludes that Umm Al Quwain has no tutors. That conclusion is half right and it is the wrong half.

Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and its private international school set is small. Most internationally schooled students from Al Raas commute out to Ajman, which is the nearest option from this part of the city, or to Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah. The pool of people living within twenty minutes of Al Raas who have taught Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 to an exam cohort is genuinely tiny, and widening the circle to the next neighbourhood adds almost nobody, because the next neighbourhood is also in Umm Al Quwain.

What families should be filtering on instead is the specification. An IGCSE is not one qualification. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run the same subjects under different codes, different paper structures and different rules, and Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C. A tutor who taught Pearson 4PH1 last year and is handed a Cambridge 0625 Extended student is competent and slightly out of position. A tutor who taught 0625 Extended for five cohorts will tell you in one sentence where candidates lose marks on Paper 4. Which of those two lives nearer Al Raas is not information worth having.

So the honest answer to the comparison between Al Raas and the area next door is that it makes no difference. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. We match your child to somebody who has taught their exact specification at their exact tier and run the session over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The market does supply in-home visits across the UAE at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour on published 2026 figures, travel folded into the rate, and this page sets out what that buys so you can judge it rather than take it on trust.

Put plainly: the area comparison is settled, and it is settled the same way from every address in the emirate. What follows is written around the IGCSE decisions that genuinely move a grade instead: the Core and Extended choice, the difference between the two boards, where marks are lost subject by subject, what the market charges, the June and November series counted backwards, how and where exams are sat in the northern emirates, and the five IGCSE passes the Ministry of Education counts towards equivalency.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raa.programmesIntro: Al Raas families arrive at one of three points in the IGCSE course, and the useful work differs sharply between them.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the IGCSE courses start
programmes.description: The years before the specification begins are where IGCSE grades are quietly decided, because algebraic fluency, reading stamina and the ability to write a structured explanation are built here rather than in Year 11. Nothing is externally assessed, so a student can look fine on school reports and arrive in Year 10 without the groundwork.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Raas family this is the cheapest intervention available, and almost nobody buys it. A student commuting to Ajman or Sharjah has limited weekday evening time, so fixing number fluency in Year 8 costs a fraction of what repairing it in Year 11 costs. One session a week for two terms at this stage changes the tier decision that follows.

programmes.name: Year 10, the first IGCSE year
programmes.description: Year 10 is where the tier decision is made and where roughly half the specification content is taught. Cambridge Core and Extended diverge here, and the choice sets the grade ceiling for two years. In the sciences the practical skills assessment begins in earnest, and in Maths the algebra that the final papers depend on is introduced.
programmes.countryNote: The Year 10 question we are asked most often from Umm Al Quwain is whether a borderline student should be entered for Core or Extended. The answer depends on evidence rather than on optimism: look at marks on Extended-standard questions under real timing, not at classwork. A tutor can supply that evidence in three or four sessions.

programmes.name: Year 11, the exam year
programmes.description: The final year is specification completion plus past-paper technique, and the second of those is where most available marks sit. Mark schemes reward specific wording, specific working and specific units, and a student who knows the content but not the scheme loses method marks across every paper. The alternative-to-practical papers reward precision about apparatus that theory revision never supplies.
programmes.countryNote: Al Raas Year 11 students sit their papers at their school's centre, which for most families is in Ajman or Sharjah rather than Umm Al Quwain. That matters because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and the zone is a property of the centre, not of where you live.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raa.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE subjects Al Raas families request, with the board codes that matter and the specific places candidates lose marks. Ask any tutor to do the same without looking it up.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: 0580 Extended reaches A* and Core stops at C, making the tier the biggest decision of Year 10. Marks go missing on transformations, bounds and the final part of multi-step problems where method marks were available for working the student did not write down.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the predictable collapse topic, and the alternative-to-practical paper punishes students who have read about circuits but never described a workable method. Pearson's paper structure and formula-sheet treatment differ from Cambridge's, which is why the code matters.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic naming are where the marks concentrate. Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 rewards precision about apparatus, observations and safety that cannot be revised from a textbook summary. Equation balancing errors cost marks in questions students otherwise understood.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Looks like recall, is marked like precision. Command terms decide the mark: describe, explain, suggest and compare each want a different answer shape. Enzymes, transport in plants and genetics are the usual points of collapse under exam timing.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: Reading questions are marked against specific skills rather than general comprehension, and directed writing is marked on audience and form as much as content. Students who write fluently but ignore the task's stated purpose lose marks that have nothing to do with their English.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: The case study decides the grade. Candidates who revise definitions and ignore the stimulus material write generic answers and score badly on the high-tariff questions. Application to the named business in front of them is the assessed skill and it responds quickly to teaching.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks and most candidates draw them carelessly: unlabelled axes, no shifted curve, no indication of the new equilibrium. Evaluation questions need a judgement supported by the analysis already written, not a new argument introduced in the last line.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and logic gates are mechanical marks that students throw away for want of practice rather than for want of understanding. Database and networking topics are usually taught thinly in small cohorts, which is exactly the shortage a commuting Umm Al Quwain student runs into.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by strong mathematicians as preparation for A-Level or the IB Diploma. It introduces calculus, trigonometric identities and logarithms early, and the step up in algebraic demand from 0580 Extended is steeper than most students expect in the first term.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Federal rules require UAE private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies whatever curriculum they are licensed to deliver. Tutoring here means supporting the school's own prescribed material, because schools may not use different content for the mandatory subjects without Ministry permission.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raa.regionsTitle: Al Raas and the areas next to it, for an IGCSE timetable
umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-al-raa.regionsIntro: Measured in the only terms that affect a weekly session: how far the school run goes and when a student is genuinely at a desk. The tutor pool does not change between these entries.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: The older quarter of Umm Al Quwain city near the creek, and the closest part of it to the Ajman road alongside Al Riqqa. A Year 11 student at an Ajman school can usually be at a desk by 17:00, which is early by this emirate's standards.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Nearest the Ajman border, which gives it the widest evening window in Umm Al Quwain. Families here often assume local tutors must therefore be easier to find, and they are not: the supply constraint is the size of the emirate, not the position within it.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: Inland and residential, with the Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road leg south as the usual bus route. That leg is the one most exposed to afternoon delay, so a 17:00 appointment set in advance tends to become a 17:25 start in practice.

regions.name: UAQ Marina
regions.note: Coastal, newer and further from both the Ajman and Sharjah roads. Arrival home from a Sharjah school typically lands between 16:00 and 17:00, so a session starts at 17:30 or later. Same boards, same shortage, a quarter of an hour more driving.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain city centre
regions.note: Where the emirate's own private schools sit, under federal Ministry of Education supervision. A locally schooled IGCSE student has a shorter day and more usable evening, though the subject range a small cohort can offer is narrower.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Deep inland, a long run to any international school. The travel premium an in-home tutor would charge is at its highest and the willing pool at its smallest, which makes the online case clearest of anywhere in the emirate.

regions.name: Ajman and Sharjah, where the exam centre usually is
regions.note: Not where you live but where the papers are sat, and therefore which Cambridge administrative zone governs the timetable your child must use. Ask the school's exams officer for the zone rather than assuming the published timetable you found applies.

Ask a school directly which board it enters candidates for, because that determines everything about the tutoring your child needs.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge tiers most IGCSE subjects. Core papers are capped at grade C; Extended papers reach A*. The decision is usually made during Year 10, sometimes earlier, and it is the single most consequential academic choice an IGCSE student's family will be consulted on, because it fixes the best possible outcome two years ahead.

Schools make the call on evidence they have, which is classwork and internal assessments. Classwork is a poor predictor, because it is untimed, often supported, and rarely set at Extended difficulty. A student who looks comfortable on Core-standard questions may be perfectly capable of Extended with a term's work on algebraic fluency, and a student entered for Extended who cannot complete a paper under timing will score worse than they would have on Core. Both errors are common and both are avoidable.

The way to resolve it is to generate real evidence: a handful of Extended-standard past-paper questions under proper timing, marked against the scheme rather than for effort. Three or four sessions produce a defensible answer. That evidence is also what a school will listen to, because it is the same kind of evidence they use. An opinion from a parent carries less weight than a marked paper.

One further consideration for Al Raas families specifically. Because most students here commute out of the emirate, a change of school between Year 9 and Year 10 is common, and a change of school can mean a change of board. A student who did Core-standard work on one specification does not automatically belong at Core on another. Ask which board and which tier the new school intends, in writing, before the entries are made.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: the same subject, two different exams
paragraphs: A parent is told their child is doing IGCSE Maths. That sentence contains almost no information. Cambridge 0580 and Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 are separate qualifications with separate papers, separate mark schemes and separate conventions, and a tutor who knows one is not automatically useful on the other.

The structural differences matter in practice. Cambridge tiers most subjects into Core and Extended; Pearson's International GCSE is untiered in most subjects and awards grades 9 to 1 rather than A* to G. Paper counts, calculator rules and the treatment of formula sheets differ. In the sciences the practical assessment is handled differently between the boards. None of this is exotic knowledge, but it is specification knowledge, and it is what separates a tutor who can lift a grade from one who can explain the topic.

The first thing to do, therefore, is find the code. It is printed on the exam entry slip, usually on the school's statement of entry, and the exams officer will confirm it. Four characters is all it takes: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1, 0620 or 4CH1. Any tutor worth hiring will ask for it unprompted, and a provider who does not ask is telling you something.

For Al Raas families there is a specific trap. Moving between schools in Ajman, Sharjah and Umm Al Quwain can mean moving between boards mid-course. A student halfway through Cambridge 0580 who arrives at a Pearson 4MA1 cohort has a real transition to manage, not a formality, and it needs a few focused sessions on the differences rather than a general tutoring arrangement.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs in the northern emirates
paragraphs: Of the competitor pages examined for this project in October 2026, three published no price at all and two quoted in US dollars. The bands below are market rates read from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They describe what the market charges, not what IB Gram charges.

Take the monthly view first, because that is how a family actually budgets. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published package rates in the market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. A family comparing those two monthly figures is comparing eight hours against eight hours, with roughly double the price for the in-home version.

Per hour, the bands run from AED 45 to 150 for a budget online tutor, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, up to AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate putting them at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500. For context on household budgets, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

What a parent can verify before paying anything: whether the rate is per hour or per session, whether it includes VAT, what a cancellation inside 24 hours costs, whether the figure rises before a series, and what happens if the tutor turns out to teach the wrong board. The last of those is the question nobody asks and the one that costs most.
