intro.heading: Start with the clock, not the subject
paragraphs: Umm Al Quwain has the smallest school-age population of the seven emirates, and UAQ Marina sits at the quieter end of it. There is no dense cluster of international campuses within ten minutes of the corniche, so almost every family running an IGCSE timetable from this address is commuting outward: south-west into Sharjah, west into Ajman, or north into Ras Al Khaimah. That single fact shapes everything else about arranging tuition here, and no competitor page on this query mentions it.

The practical consequence is a compressed evening. A Year 10 student leaving an Al Layyah or Al Nahda campus at 14:45 is rarely home before 16:00, and in the heavier November and January traffic weeks that can slip past 16:30. Add food, prayer, a shower and the twenty minutes it takes any teenager to stop being a passenger and start being a student, and the first genuinely usable slot of the day begins around 17:00. Lose that hour to a tutor stuck on the Emirates Road and the session either shrinks or does not happen.

An in-home tutor serving UAQ Marina has to absorb that commute twice. Published rates for in-home one-to-one work in the UAE reflect it: the market quotes roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor teaching the same hour over video. The difference is not better teaching. It is petrol, parking and an hour of someone's evening, paid for by you.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; in-person visits are an India-only service, and saying so plainly is more useful to you than pretending otherwise. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, which is why a UAQ Marina family can book a Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 specialist for 17:30 on a Tuesday rather than accepting whichever generalist is willing to drive up from Sharjah. The trade you are making is a shared screen instead of a shared table, and in exchange you get a subject specialist, a shorter notice period and no travel surcharge.

There is a second scheduling trap worth naming before you book anything. School revision clubs, coursework catch-up sessions and subject surgeries at Sharjah and Ajman campuses are timetabled immediately after the last lesson, because that is when the majority of the cohort is still on site. A student who has to catch the Umm Al Quwain bus cannot attend them, which means the support the school fee already paid for is structurally unavailable to this household. That gap, not a weak teacher, is what most UAQ Marina families are actually trying to fill.

What follows is written for the UAQ Marina school run specifically: where this neighbourhood's students actually study, what time the day ends, when a session realistically fits, what the market charges, how the two exam boards differ, and how the June and November series work backwards from tonight.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-uaq-ma.programmesIntro: Most UAQ Marina students reach IGCSE through a British-curriculum primary and lower-secondary route, then split towards A Level or the IB Diploma at 16. programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE decide how much ground a student has to make up later. Algebraic fluency, the structure of a scientific explanation and the habit of answering the command word rather than the topic are all built here. Work at this stage is cheap compared with Year 11 remediation, and it is the point at which a weak start in a new school is still invisible on paper.
programmes.countryNote: For UAQ Marina families this is also the window in which a school change is least disruptive. Students moving between a Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah campus at Year 7 or 8 can absorb a curriculum change; the same move in Year 10 means arriving mid-syllabus with coursework already underway and a different exam board in play.

programmes.name: International GCSE, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight or nine subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal written papers. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel both run the qualification in the UAE, with different paper structures and different tiering rules for the same named subject. The grade on the certificate is what the Ministry of Education counts for equivalency, and what a sixth form reads when it offers a place.
programmes.countryNote: A UAQ Marina student is often one of very few candidates from this emirate in their cohort, which means school revision clubs are built around the majority commute, not yours. A 17:00 online session is the realistic alternative to a 15:30 after-school club that your child would have to miss the bus to attend.

programmes.name: The move into sixth form at 16
programmes.description: The step from IGCSE into either A Level or the IB Diploma Programme is the single largest jump in difficulty most students meet. Extended-tier IGCSE Maths covers less than the first term of Analysis and Approaches; IGCSE Chemistry treats organic reactions as recall where the Diploma treats them as mechanism. The students who cope have usually closed that gap deliberately rather than hoped it would close.
programmes.countryNote: Sixth-form choice is geographically harder from Umm Al Quwain than from Dubai, because the shortlist of campuses within an hour that run the full IB Diploma is short. umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-uaq-ma.subjectsIntro: These are the IGCSE subjects UAQ Marina families book most often, with what each one actually assesses and the specific place marks go missing. Every subject is taught from your child's own board and syllabus code, not a generic version of it.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher tier
subjects.description: Two papers on both boards, no coursework. Extended and Higher tier questions carry method marks that are lost silently: unsimplified surds, a bearing measured from the wrong north line, a probability tree that never gets multiplied along the branch. Most of the recoverable marks in this subject are presentation, not understanding.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Mechanics and electricity carry the heaviest mark load and produce the most dropped marks. Students lose them on units, on describing a graph instead of reading a value from it, and on practical questions that ask for a control variable rather than a conclusion. Required-practical recall is examined in the written papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and the qualitative-analysis tables are where grades are made. The commonest avoidable loss is a balanced equation written without state symbols where the mark scheme demands them, closely followed by describing a colour change without naming the species responsible for it.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the marks turn on precision of language. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance diagrams reward students who use the examiner's vocabulary exactly: diffusion is not osmosis, and a monohybrid cross needs the gametes shown before the ratio counts.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with speaking endorsement
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, a summary task with a strict word allowance, and extended writing judged on register as much as accuracy. UAQ Marina students who speak fluent English often underperform here because they write how they talk; the summary task punishes that harder than any other component.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
subjects.description: Directed writing and a composition, both marked against structure and effect rather than content volume. The single most common cause of a lost grade is a response that narrates the passage back instead of analysing how the writer achieves an effect on the reader.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450 / Edexcel 4BS1)
subjects.description: Case-study papers where the command word decides the mark ceiling. Explain earns two marks for a developed point; evaluate requires a judgement with a stated criterion. Students who learn definitions and ignore command terms cap themselves at around a grade C regardless of effort.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is the differentiator: axes labelled, curves shifted rather than slid along, and the new equilibrium marked. The data-response paper rewards students who quote a figure from the extract in support of every claim they make.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478 / 0984)
subjects.description: Theory paper plus a problem-solving paper. Binary, hexadecimal and logic gates are quick wins; pseudocode under exam conditions is where the time goes. Trace tables written neatly earn marks even when the final output is wrong.

subjects.name: Arabic as a Second Language (Cambridge 0544)
subjects.description: Reading, writing and directed response in Modern Standard Arabic. For many internationally schooled students in Umm Al Quwain this runs alongside a Ministry-mandated Arabic stream at school, and the two have different expectations. Tuition here is about script fluency and controlled sentence patterns, not conversation.

sections.heading: What a UAQ Marina family is really asking for
paragraphs: The phrase IGCSE home tutor in UAQ Marina almost never means someone who will sit in your living room. It means someone who will teach your child in your home, in the hour between the school run and bedtime, without that hour being eaten by a drive. Those are two different requirements, and only one of them has anything to do with geography.

Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and its internationally schooled students are spread thin across campuses in three neighbouring emirates. That means the pool of people living within a twenty-minute drive of UAQ Marina who can teach Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 to Extended tier is genuinely small. A family insisting on physical attendance is not choosing between specialists; it is choosing between whoever is available and nobody.

Online one-to-one changes the question from who is nearby to who is right. The Marina family that wants a Physics specialist who has marked hundreds of 0625 Paper 4 scripts can have one at 17:30 on a Tuesday. The lesson happens in the home, at the dining table, with the parent in earshot if they want to be. What does not happen is a tutor arriving at a UAE address, because IB Gram does not run that service here.

Read the rest of this page as the honest version of the answer: what the commute does to your evening, what the market charges for each option, how the two IGCSE boards differ, and what the June and November series require of you between now and then.

sections.heading: The school run from UAQ Marina and when a session actually fits
paragraphs: Scheduling tuition from this neighbourhood is an arithmetic problem with three terms: when the school day ends, how long the return journey takes, and how much recovery time a fourteen-year-old needs before anything useful can happen. Get any of the three wrong and the first session is fine, the fourth is a fight and the eighth is cancelled.

The table below sets out the four routes UAQ Marina students commute on, with indicative one-way drive times and the earliest session start that has historically worked for families on each. Times are indicative rather than guaranteed, because term-time traffic on the Emirates Road and the Sharjah ring roads varies by week and by prayer timing, and because school finish times differ by year group at most campuses.

Two patterns come out of it. Ajman-bound students get the most usable evening and can often start at 16:00 or 16:30, which matters enormously in Year 11 when a second subject has to fit somewhere. Dubai-bound students have the narrowest window of all and should be booked for 18:00 or later, with a weekend slot carrying the heavier lifting rather than a weekday one.

The reason this section exists is that no competing page on this query mentions it. Rate pages and tutor-list pages treat scheduling as a footnote. For a household in the northern emirates, it is the whole problem, and it is also the thing in-home tutoring makes worse rather than better.

sections.heading: What IGCSE tuition costs around Umm Al Quwain, cheapest option first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most families start in practice. A university-student tutor working online advertises from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour: Tutopiya publishes rates from about AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from about AED 45 to 65. That buys homework supervision and company. It does not usually buy someone who knows that Cambridge 0620 Paper 6 is the alternative-to-practical paper.

The next band up, a qualified subject tutor teaching online, runs about AED 150 to 300 an hour. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Above that sits the specialist band at roughly AED 200 to 450 and beyond, with TutorChase quoting around AED 270 and premium named tutors reaching AED 650 at the top of the range reported by BartyED.

In-home one-to-one is a separate line rather than a tier, because what you pay extra for is travel. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. From an Umm Al Quwain address, the travel premium is larger than it would be in Dubai and the specialist pool it reaches is smaller.

All figures above are market rates published by other providers, quoted so you can calibrate a quote you receive elsewhere. They are not IB Gram's price list. Our own position starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about how many hours the diagnosis actually justifies, which in most cases is fewer than a family expects.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: find out before you book anything
paragraphs: Parents in the northern emirates frequently do not know which board their child sits, because schools talk about IGCSE as though it were one qualification. It is two systems with different paper structures, different tiering rules and different calendars, and booking a tutor without knowing which one is the single commonest waste of money on this query.

The fastest way to find out is the statement of entry, which carries the board, the subject code and the paper numbers. Failing that, the front cover of a past paper in your child's folder will say Cambridge Assessment International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Ask the subject teacher directly if neither is to hand; it is a thirty-second question with a large consequence.

The practical differences matter in teaching. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended with a capped grade on Core; Edexcel tiers Maths into Foundation and Higher and treats most sciences as single tier. Cambridge runs its own alternative-to-practical papers; Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Cambridge offers a June and a November series to UAE candidates, while Edexcel International GCSE runs May or June and November.

One Cambridge administrative detail is worth knowing because it has consequences nobody can fix afterwards. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one. If your child is entered as a private candidate, confirm the zone with the centre rather than assuming.

sections.heading: The exam series, counted backwards from a Tuesday evening in UAQ Marina
paragraphs: Exam-session awareness is almost entirely absent from the pages competing for this search, which is odd, because it is the only part of the process with fixed dates attached. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Umm Al Quwain family should be planning around it.

Working backwards is more useful than working forwards. Final entries close months before the papers, and that deadline is set by the centre rather than by you, so the school's internal cut-off is usually weeks earlier again. Mocks land roughly a term ahead and are the last honest diagnostic you get. The eight weeks before a series are for paper technique under timing, not for meeting new content, which means any content gap has to be closed before that window opens.

The Pearson calendar gives a worked example with real dates, because those dates are published. The November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so always open the live official timetable rather than trusting a date restated on a tutoring page.

For a family in Umm Al Quwain the operational point is simpler than the calendar. If your child is in Year 11 and sitting the June series, the content work belongs to this term and the paper work belongs to next. If the diagnosis says there is a content gap and there are fewer than eight weeks left, the honest advice is usually to narrow the plan to two topics and protect the marks that are reachable rather than to add a third session a week.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school and who licenses your tutor
paragraphs: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae describes as playing a supervisory role for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is different from Dubai, where the Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education, and from Abu Dhabi, where the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools.

The distinction has practical weight for a commuting family. If your child studies in Sharjah, the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates that school and approves its fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. If the campus is in Ras Al Khaimah, the emirate's Department of Knowledge does the same. So an Umm Al Quwain household can easily be a Ministry of Education household by address and a SPEA household by school, and the inspection reports, fee approvals and complaint routes follow the school rather than the home.

Tutor licensing is a separate and federal question. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service called Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with a stated two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow. First, anyone telling you a permit costs money or is optional is wrong on both counts: individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion. Second, do not ask for your child's own classroom teacher privately. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid tutoring of students at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every UAE private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver. The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. This is the part of the week families from abroad are least prepared for and the part where marks quietly disappear.

The Dubai regulator publishes the most detailed version of these requirements, and it is worth reading even if your child studies in Sharjah or Ajman, because it shows how seriously the mandatory stream is treated. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

The same guidance sets language of instruction: Standard Arabic for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in moral, social and cultural studies. It also states that using different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any tutor describes material for these subjects.

What that means for tuition is narrow and honest. A tutor can build script fluency, vocabulary and sentence control in Arabic, and can help a student understand and revise the content their school has taught in Islamic Education and Social Studies. A tutor cannot supply a parallel syllabus, and should not pretend the mandatory stream is optional. For a UAQ Marina student carrying nine IGCSE subjects plus the mandatory stream, the useful conversation is about where the hours come from, not about adding more of them.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do, and what the Ministry counts later
paragraphs: IGCSE is lighter on coursework than the IB Diploma, but the honesty line still matters, and it matters more every year as more of the work happens on a screen. A tutor teaches, explains, sets practice, marks and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce the work. On this site that is a rule rather than a preference, and it is worth saying out loud because at least one provider ranking for UAE tutoring queries sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

In practice the line is easy to hold and easy to see. A tutor annotating your child's own essay with where the argument loses the reader is teaching. A tutor supplying paragraphs for that essay is not. A tutor working through a past-paper question your child has attempted is teaching. A tutor completing a piece of assessed coursework is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, not on the tutor.

The other long-horizon question families in Umm Al Quwain ask is what these grades are worth locally. For the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects, which is a detail at least one ranking competitor publishes incorrectly as a six-subject rule.

For the American track the same clarification sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so do not accept one from a tutoring page, including ours. Equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutoring service performs or guarantees, and the only safe place to verify your child's specific position is the Ministry's own channel.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: The useful first message is short: year group, board, subject code, school, and the time the school bus gets back to UAQ Marina. Those five facts are enough to shortlist a tutor properly. Without the code we are guessing between Cambridge 0580 and Edexcel 4MA1, and the past papers differ.

process.title: A free trial lesson in your real slot
process.description: The trial runs at the time you would actually book, so you find out whether a 17:00 session works for your child after a Sharjah commute rather than whether it works in theory. There is no payment at this stage and no obligation afterwards.

process.title: A marked paper before a plan
process.description: The tutor sets one timed section from a past paper and marks it against the real mark scheme. That single document usually reorders the priority list, because the topics a student feels weakest in are often not the topics costing the marks.

process.title: A weekly slot and a written note
process.description: Lessons settle into a fixed time, with a short note after each one saying what was covered and what was set. For a commuting household the note matters: it means you do not have to interrogate a tired teenager to find out whether the hour was worth it.

process.title: Review against the series, then stop or continue
process.description: Before each series we review whether the hours are still earning their keep. Sometimes the answer is fewer sessions, sometimes a different subject, occasionally a different tutor. Tuition that never gets reviewed turns into a standing order, which is the commonest way families here waste money.

whyPoints.title: The specialist, not the nearest person
whyPoints.description: From an Umm Al Quwain address the pool of people who can teach Extended-tier Cambridge Chemistry within driving distance is small. Online delivery replaces that pool with a national one, which is the whole argument for the format rather than a consolation for it.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around your commute
whyPoints.description: Slots are set after the school bus, not before it. Families running to Ajman usually take 16:30, Sharjah families 17:30, and Dubai families a weekend morning. We would rather move the slot than watch a student arrive at a lesson still in uniform and unable to think.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the exact syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 are both IGCSE Physics and they are not the same teaching job. Matching on code rather than on subject name is the least glamorous thing we do and the one that most reliably prevents a wasted first month.

whyPoints.title: Market rates published, our own hours argued down
whyPoints.description: The rate tables on this page are other providers' published figures, cited so you can judge a quote. On our side the conversation usually goes the other way: a marked paper often shows that two topics and six sessions will do what a family assumed needed a year.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not do
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses, does not write assessed work, does not hold any regulator's accreditation, and does not publish grade guarantees. Those four sentences disqualify us for some families, which is better for everyone than discovering it in month two.

faqs.question: Can I actually get a tutor to come to my home in UAQ Marina?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and we do not send tutors to any UAE address. Independent in-home tutors do work in the northern emirates, and market rates for that service run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is priced in. From UAQ Marina the travel element is larger than it would be in Dubai and the specialist pool it reaches is smaller, so our view is that the same hour spent online with a subject specialist is the better purchase. You decide after a free trial lesson, not before.

faqs.question: What time can a session realistically start after the Sharjah school run?
faqs.answer: Around 17:00 on a normal school night. A student leaving an Al Layyah or Al Nahda campus in the mid-afternoon is usually back in UAQ Marina between 15:45 and 16:30, and the gap after that goes on food, prayer and the twenty minutes it takes to stop being a passenger. Ajman-bound students often manage 16:00 or 16:30, Ras Al Khaimah students around 16:45, and anyone commuting to Dubai should be booked for 18:00 or a weekend morning instead.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series will my child sit in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and again in November. The February and March series you may see mentioned online is offered to India only and does not apply to candidates sitting in the UAE. June is the main series for most Year 11 cohorts here, with November used as the resit route. Confirm the exact papers and dates against the board's live official timetable and your child's statement of entry.

faqs.question: How does a UAQ Marina parent check which IGCSE board their child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Look at the statement of entry first: it carries the board name, the subject code and the paper numbers. If you cannot find it, open a past paper in your child's folder and read the front cover, which will say either Cambridge Assessment International Education or Pearson Edexcel. If neither is available, ask the subject teacher directly. It takes half a minute and it decides which past papers are worth practising, which is why booking a tutor without that answer is the commonest way money gets wasted on this search.

faqs.question: Is online tuition genuinely workable for a Year 11 student in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: It is workable when the session is structured and the student has a quiet surface and a charged device. The things that make it work are a shared screen for annotating a past paper, a fixed weekly time, and a tutor who sets written work between lessons. The things that break it are a bedroom door open to a younger sibling, a phone within reach, and a slot placed before the student has eaten. From an Umm Al Quwain address the alternative is often no subject specialist at all, which is a worse trade than a screen.

faqs.question: Does my private tutor need a permit to teach my child in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring is regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Can I ask my child's own schoolteacher to tutor privately in the evening?
faqs.answer: It is the wrong thing to ask for, even when the teacher is willing. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that similarly bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. The arrangement also creates a conflict around internal assessment and predicted grades. A different specialist, with no stake in your child's school marks, gives you a cleaner second opinion.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a slipping Year 10 student actually need?
faqs.answer: Usually one, in one subject, for a term. Families arriving at this search often expect to buy three or four hours a week across every subject, and that is rarely what a marked paper justifies. One hour a week in the subject where marks are measurably leaking, with written work set between sessions, moves more than four scattered hours do. If the diagnosis shows gaps in two subjects, two separate specialists on two evenings beats one generalist covering both, which is only possible because the lessons are online.

faqs.question: What does the in-home premium actually buy in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: It buys the tutor's travel, and a physical presence in the room. Published market figures put in-home one-to-one at roughly AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Dubai rate work, with independent home tutors quoting AED 200 to 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages in this market run about AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. From UAQ Marina the drive is longer, so the premium is bigger and the choice of specialist is narrower.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my daughter's Arabic and Islamic Education lessons too?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are worth stating. A tutor can build script fluency, vocabulary and controlled sentence patterns in Arabic, and can help a student revise and understand content their school has already taught in Islamic Education and Social Studies. What a tutor cannot do is supply a parallel syllabus: the Dubai regulator's guidance states that using different or additional content for the mandatory subjects without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. These subjects are compulsory in UAE private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach.

faqs.question: Will IGCSE grades from a Sharjah or Ajman school count for a UAE university?
faqs.answer: The Ministry of Education runs an equivalency process, and the British-track requirement is published: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One competing page states a six-subject rule, which is wrong. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs, so verify your child's position through the official channel.

faqs.question: With eight weeks left before the June papers, is starting now worth the money?
faqs.answer: It is not too late to protect marks, but the plan has to change shape. Eight weeks is a paper-technique window, not a content window, so the right move is to narrow to the two topics with the largest recoverable mark load and drill them under exam timing. That starts with a marked past paper, because the topics a student feels weakest in are often not the ones costing marks. What does not work in eight weeks is adding a third weekly session and attempting the whole syllabus again.

faqs.question: Should one tutor take both Maths 0580 and Physics 0625, or two specialists?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being careful about it. A strong Maths and Physics teacher genuinely exists, and for a Year 10 student needing algebraic fluency across both, one tutor can be more coherent than two. In Year 11, with two sets of papers, two mark schemes and two required-practical lists to drill, two specialists usually produce better results. Online delivery is what makes the second specialist available from Umm Al Quwain at all, so the constraint is your evening rather than the local supply.

faqs.question: If the first tutor does not suit my child, how quickly can we swap?
faqs.answer: Say so early and we change the match. A mismatch is usually visible in two sessions: the student goes quiet, the written work stops coming back, or the tutor is teaching at the wrong level of abstraction for how this child thinks. None of that is a failure of effort and none of it improves by waiting. We would rather move a student in week two than defend a pairing into week eight, and the free trial exists precisely so the first pairing is an informed guess rather than a blind one.

faqs.question: Do you publish a price list for IGCSE tuition in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: The figures on this page are other providers' published market rates, cited so you can judge any quote you receive. Our own conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a marked paper, because the honest number depends on how many hours the diagnosis justifies rather than on a published tier. That is also why we would rather talk about six sessions on two topics than sell a year of weekly hours, and why we review the plan before each exam series instead of letting it run.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-uaq-ma.closingHeading: Book the trial in the slot you would actually use
umm-al-quwain/igcse-home-tutor-in-uaq-ma.closingBody: If your child commutes out of UAQ Marina to a Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah campus, the single most useful thing you can do is try a lesson at the real time rather than a convenient one. Send us the year group, the board, the subject code and the time the school run gets home, and we will put a specialist in front of your child in that exact slot for a free trial. After that you will have a marked paper, a short written note and an honest view of how many hours this actually needs, which is usually fewer than you expect.

intro.heading: Price the hour honestly, starting with who is driving
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for queries like this publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Umm Al Quwain family transacts in. So the first thing this page does is put the market in dirhams with the source of every band named. The second is to explain what changes the number here specifically, because this emirate's geography does something to tutoring costs that Dubai's does not.

Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and it has no large international-school estate of its own. Most internationally schooled students here travel out: to Sharjah's Muwaileh and University City campuses, to Ajman, or north towards Ras Al Khaimah. That commute is the single most important economic fact about tutoring in this emirate, and it works in two directions. It compresses the evening a lesson has to fit into, and it means that any tutor who physically attends the house is driving in from another emirate.

That drive is inside the price whether or not anyone itemises it. A visiting tutor who spends fifty minutes travelling from Al Nahda or Ajman and fifty minutes going home has committed two hours and fifty minutes to deliver sixty minutes of teaching. No reasonable person does that for the price of an hour, and they do not. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with visiting home tutors advertised to AED 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online.

What a family in Al Salamah or UAQ Marina should take from that is not that in-home tutoring is overpriced. It is that the premium buys travel rather than teaching, and whether that is worth paying depends entirely on whether a person physically in the room is the thing this particular student needs. For a Year 7 who will not stay on task without supervision, it often is. For a Year 11 preparing for a June series with a marked script to analyse, it usually is not, and the same money spent on more teaching hours does more useful work than the same money spent on somebody's drive.

The rest of the page is the detail: the rate bands with sources, what moves a quote here, how session length changes the per-hour figure, how hourly, block and monthly billing actually behave, why the cheapest hour is frequently the dearest per mark recovered, what a free trial should settle before money moves, and who is legally permitted to charge for lessons in the UAE at all. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Two examined routes and one continuation route matter to an Umm Al Quwain family paying for IGCSE support, and the differences change what an hour should cost and contain.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two-year courses examined by external papers in a June series and a November series, with syllabuses identified by four-digit codes such as 0580 mathematics and 0625 physics. Many subjects are tiered Core or Extended, and the tier caps the achievable grade. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students usually sit papers at a centre in another emirate, because their school is in another emirate. That changes exam-day logistics and it also means the entry decisions, including tier, are made by a school the family travels to rather than one down the road. Confirm both in writing early.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other main international route, with codes such as 4MA1 for mathematics and examinations in May or June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.
programmes.countryNote: Families who change campus between emirates sometimes change board mid-course, which is a technique job rather than a restart. It does, however, change the price of support: a term of transition work on paper structure and formula provision is a defined block with a defined cost rather than an open commitment.

programmes.name: IB Diploma and International A Level
programmes.description: The two routes an IGCSE student continues into at sixteen, both of which price above IGCSE in every published rate table. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutoring is advertised at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, so the cost of support rises at exactly the point family budgets are already stretched by sixth-form fees.
programmes.countryNote: The Core or Extended decision taken in Year 10 reaches into this stage, and so does its cost. Moving a student up a tier in Year 10 is a planned block of Extended-only content; discovering in Year 12 that the foundation is not there is the expensive version of the same problem.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Rates vary by subject more than families expect, because the pool of tutors varies. The subjects below are the ones Umm Al Quwain households ask about, with a note on why each prices where it does.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or tiered by board
subjects.description: The most commonly requested subject and therefore the most competitively priced, sitting at the lower end of the qualified-tutor band. Extended-tier work draws on a smaller pool and prices above Core. Marks go missing in multi-step questions with no working shown and in algebra under time pressure.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside mathematics by students heading for a mathematics-heavy sixth form. The pool of tutors covering it in the northern emirates is thin, so it reliably prices above standard mathematics regardless of format. Sequencing matters: secure algebra from the main syllabus first.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 and 4PH1)
subjects.description: Prices in the middle of the specialist band because the pool is narrower than mathematics. Students lose marks describing rather than explaining, and computing a graph gradient without interpreting it. Equation rearrangement under time is technique, and technique blocks are the cheapest effective purchase here.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic with units carried correctly is the highest-value repair available and it is short work. Extended-only electrolysis, stoichiometry and organic content is where a Core-prepared student stalls, which makes a late tier change an expensive decision rather than a free one.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Content-heavy and vocabulary-precise, so a cheap generalist hour often produces less movement here than in mathematics. Data questions reward reading the axes before writing, and command-term discipline decides more of the grade than recall does. Both are trainable in a short block.

subjects.name: English as a First Language (0500)
subjects.description: Widely covered, so competitively priced, and the summary question is the most teachable high-value component on the paper. Marks are lost by copying rather than compressing. A student at a grade 5 or 6 frequently recovers marks faster here than in any science subject.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Pricing varies most in this subject because the pool is wide and the quality range is wider. Ask what a prospective tutor has actually taught to the specific paper, because general English conversation practice and examined second-language technique are different products at similar prices.

subjects.name: Economics (0455) and Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: Thinner pools than the sciences in this part of the UAE, so rates sit above mathematics for comparable experience. Diagram accuracy and applied judgement carry the marks; describing a business or restating both sides of an argument does not, and that distinction is quick to teach.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Prices above average because fewer tutors teach the board's own pseudocode conventions rather than a programming language. Trace tables and data representation are predictable marks. A tutor fluent in Python who has never read the specification's pseudocode rules is a poor purchase at any rate.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Private schools must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed curriculum, with separate provision for Arabic speakers and non-Arabic speakers. Support priced for first-language Arabic is wasted on a student placed in an acquisition stream, so confirm the stream in writing first.

sections.heading: The market in dirhams, and what sits inside the hour
paragraphs: Here is the published market, band by band, with the source of each figure. Budget online tutoring and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour: EdFlik publishes from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one, travel inside the number, runs roughly AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table giving 180 to 350 and visiting home tutors advertised to 500. IGCSE and IB specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named tutors are advertised higher, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly shapes also exist in the market: packages of around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider named. None of them is an IB Gram price list.

What matters as much as the number is what the number includes, and this is where comparison breaks down in practice. Two quotes at AED 200 can differ substantially: one covers sixty minutes of teaching and nothing else, the other covers the session plus marking a paper the student submits between sessions, a written note to the parent, and the tutor reading the school's scheme of work. Ask what is inside the hour before comparing hours.

Our own position, stated plainly rather than buried: we start with a free trial lesson taught by the tutor who would take the course, with no card required and no condition attached, and we quote a plan after it. The reason is not coyness. The number of sessions a student needs depends on whether the lost marks are content, technique or timing, and that cannot be known before someone has read a marked script. Quoting first and diagnosing later is how families end up abandoning a plan halfway.

sections.heading: The travel premium from Umm Al Quwain, costed rather than asserted
paragraphs: This emirate pays the clearest travel premium in the country, and the arithmetic is worth doing once properly. An Umm Al Quwain household has no large international-school estate on its doorstep, so a tutor with IGCSE experience is almost certainly living in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah. From Al Nahda or Muwaileh to Al Salamah is a meaningful drive, and from either to Falaj Al Mualla is a long one. Add the return journey and a sixty-minute lesson consumes most of a working evening.

Nobody absorbs that for free, and nobody should be expected to. A tutor committing two and a half to three hours to deliver one hour of teaching has to price the whole commitment, which is why the in-home band in every published table sits above the online band for comparable experience. The number is not a mark-up for quality; it is a payment for road.

The honest way to compare the two is cost per teaching minute, and the exercise reframes the decision immediately. At AED 350 an hour in-home, a family spending AED 1,400 a month buys four hours of teaching. At AED 220 an hour online, the same AED 1,400 buys six hours and a bit. The question is then whether two additional teaching hours a month are worth less to this student than having an adult physically present. For some students they are, and that is a legitimate answer.

A third option exists and deserves honest treatment: a group class at a centre in Ajman or Sharjah. Per hour it is the cheapest of the three, and for a student who needs routine and company it can do real work. The costs people forget are the drive there and back, which lands on the family rather than the tutor, and the fact that a class of eight from four different schools teaches a syllabus rather than this student's marked script. For a Year 11 three months from a series with a specific pattern of lost marks, that is the wrong product at any price.

sections.heading: Six things that move a quote here, and three that do not
paragraphs: Families often assume the rate is a fixed property of a tutor. It is not; it responds to six things, and knowing them lets you change the number rather than just accept it. The tier is first and least expected: Extended-tier work in a tiered subject draws on a smaller pool than Core work and prices above it. Subject scarcity is second, and in the northern emirates Additional Mathematics 0606, computer science and economics all sit above mathematics for comparable experience.

Third is proximity to a series. Demand concentrates from February and again from October, and the same hour costs more and is harder to book in those windows than in September. Starting in the autumn term is the single cheapest decision available to a family. Fourth is session length, which changes the figure in both directions: ninety minutes usually costs less per teaching minute than forty-five, because fixed preparation spreads further.

Fifth is what is included. A quote covering teaching only is not comparable to one covering teaching plus marking a submitted paper, a written parent note and reading the school's scheme of work. Sixth is commitment shape: a block of eight quoted as a block is frequently priced differently from eight sessions bought one at a time, and the block also forces a review that an open arrangement never gets.

Three things do not move the number as much as parents expect. The student's current grade does not, because a 3 and a 6 both take an hour to teach even though they need different plans. Having two children does not halve it, particularly where they sit different boards, because Cambridge and Pearson preparation genuinely differ. And geography within this emirate does not affect an online rate at all, which is the whole point: a family in Falaj Al Mualla pays the same as one in Al Haditha, which is not true of any in-home arrangement.

sections.heading: Session length economics: forty-five, sixty and ninety minutes
paragraphs: Session length is the lever families use least and that changes value most, partly because the published rate is almost always quoted per hour regardless of how the hour is actually sold. The underlying economics are simple. Every session carries fixed costs that do not scale with length: reading what the student submitted, planning the session, writing the note afterwards. Spread across ninety minutes those costs are proportionally smaller than across forty-five.

That does not make ninety minutes the right answer. A fourteen-year-old working on algebra at the end of a day that started with a bus to Sharjah at half past six has a concentration limit, and teaching past it is paying for nothing. Forty-five minutes of engaged work beats ninety minutes of which the last thirty are endured. The right length is the longest one the student can actually hold, which a trial lesson establishes better than a conversation does.

Length also has to match the task. Single-topic repair works well in forty-five minutes. Whole-paper practice does not fit at all: a Paper 4 takes most of an hour to sit, so a session that includes sitting it, marking it against the scheme and discussing the pattern needs ninety. Technique blocks before a series are therefore usually ninety-minute shapes, while mid-year content support is usually sixty.

The pattern that works for most Umm Al Quwain households, given the commute, is a sixty-minute weekday session plus a ninety-minute weekend session in the term before a series, rather than two weekday sessions. The weekday slot keeps momentum and the weekend slot carries the full-paper work the evening cannot hold. It also respects the thing a week audit always reveals here: there are fewer usable weekday evening hours than anyone plans for.

sections.heading: Hourly, block or monthly: how each billing shape behaves
paragraphs: The three ways tutoring is sold produce different behaviour, and the behaviour matters more than the headline figure. Pay-as-you-go hourly is the most flexible and the least likely to produce a result, because nothing forces anyone to ask whether it is working. Weeks accumulate, the total is never visible in one place, and a family discovers in March that they have spent more than a block would have cost without a single review.

A block of a defined number of sessions with a stated target and finish date is the shape we recommend for nearly every Year 11 request. The total is known before it starts. There is a halfway checkpoint with the student's own marked work in front of everyone. And it ends, which means somebody has to decide whether to continue. That forced decision is the feature, not an inconvenience.

Monthly packages are common in the market and they work well where they are honest about two things: what happens to unused sessions, and what notice ends the arrangement. Packages seen in the market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four in-home two-hour sessions. Ask both questions before paying. A package that forfeits unused sessions across a Ramadan month or an exam-leave fortnight costs more than the headline implies.

Two more questions belong in any pricing conversation and they are rarely asked. First, whether the quoted dirham figure includes value added tax: we will not state the UAE tax treatment of tuition as fact without a Federal Tax Authority citation, so the right question is simply whether the number you were given is the number you pay. Second, the cancellation and rescheduling terms, which matter far more here than in Dubai because the school run from this emirate is long enough that lessons genuinely do need moving.

sections.heading: Why the cheapest hour is often the dearest per mark
paragraphs: The cheapest band in the market is real and it is sometimes the right purchase. A capable student who needs company, routine and somebody to check that work is done can be well served at the budget end, and spending four times as much on a specialist would be waste. The error is using a budget hour for a diagnostic problem, which is where almost all wasted tutoring spend in this market goes.

The arithmetic is unforgiving. A student losing eighteen marks on Paper 4, of which twelve are going to command words and timing, needs somebody who can read the script, name the pattern and drill the shape of the answer. That is six to ten sessions and the marks come back. The same student with a tutor working through the textbook from chapter one gets a pleasant twenty sessions, no script analysis and the same eighteen marks lost in the series. At AED 100 an hour that is AED 2,000 for nothing; at AED 250 an hour the effective version is AED 2,000 for the marks.

So the metric worth using is cost per mark recovered, not cost per hour, and it can be estimated honestly before committing. Ask a prospective tutor: how many sessions, what is the target in marks or in a named component, and what evidence will exist at the halfway point. A tutor who answers all three precisely has done the diagnosis you are paying for. One who cannot has not looked at the script.

There is a related trap at the other end. Premium rates are advertised up to AED 650 an hour, and at that level the premium is the individual rather than extra service. For a student at a grade 6 needing the last marks in one component, a small number of hours with the right person can be worth it. For a student with two years of missing algebra, it is the most expensive possible way to do work that patience and sequencing would do better. Match the tier of spend to the problem, not to the anxiety.

sections.heading: What a free trial should settle before any money moves
paragraphs: A trial lesson is worth something only if it answers questions. Ours is free, requires no card and carries no condition, and it is taught by the tutor who would take the course rather than by a salesperson. The point is diagnosis: by the end, somebody should be able to say what the lost marks are going to and roughly how many sessions it takes to get them back.

Four things a trial should establish, and they are worth asking for explicitly whoever you trial with. Whether the tutor has read the student's marked script and can name the pattern in it. Whether the student can work in this format, which for live video means writing on a shared document and talking while being watched. What the target is, stated in marks or in a named component. And how many sessions, with a halfway checkpoint.

Two things a trial should not do. It should not require payment details to begin, because a free offer with a condition attached is not free and the condition belongs on the same screen as the word. And it should not end with a recommendation to buy regardless of what the lesson showed. Sometimes the honest outcome is that a group class in Ajman would serve this student better, that the school's own support sessions have not been used yet, or that the student needs sleep and triage more than teaching.

On data, because lead forms for school-age children collect sensitive information: we ask for what is needed to match a tutor and nothing more, we state why, and personal data can be deleted on request. The UAE's personal data protection framework under Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 sits behind that, and a privacy link belongs on every page that asks a parent for anything. No child's school report, grades and photograph should ever be collected by anybody without a stated purpose.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge for lessons, and what a legitimate arrangement looks like
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is the part of pricing nobody advertises. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Two consequences follow for a parent comparing quotes. First, the permit costs the tutor nothing, so a rate justified by licensing fees is justified by something that does not exist. Second, individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount should be quoted by anybody, including by us. The official application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fees and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

There is a related boundary worth knowing. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported as also barring serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document, but never pursue an arrangement marketed as your child's own teacher, privately. For an Umm Al Quwain family whose child attends school in another emirate, this is a live question rather than a theoretical one.

A legitimate arrangement therefore looks like this: a tutor who can confirm they hold the permit, a clear statement of what the quoted dirham figure covers and whether it is the figure you pay, written cancellation and rescheduling terms, and no claim of regulator approval. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, any emirate regulator, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office or centre. Any page implying otherwise is making a claim worth checking before money moves.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects at Core and Extended tier for Cambridge and at Foundation and Higher tier for Pearson Edexcel. Each works from the published assessment objectives for the specific syllabus, not from a general idea of what Year 10 and Year 11 cover.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE tutor is being hired to do
paragraphs: An IGCSE is not one qualification. It is a set of separate specifications, each with its own code, its own papers and its own mark scheme, sat by candidates at two different tiers under two different grading scales. A family in Umm Al Quwain whose child attends a British-curriculum school in Sharjah or Ajman may have a son sitting Cambridge Mathematics 0580 at Extended tier and a daughter sitting Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics A 4MA1 at Higher tier. The subject is maths in both cases. The papers, the question styles and the grade scales are not the same, and a tutor who treats them as the same wastes the hour.

So the first job is identification. Before a single topic is taught, the syllabus code has to be confirmed, the tier has to be confirmed, and the components have to be listed: how many written papers, whether a practical paper or an alternative-to-practical paper is sat, whether there is a speaking endorsement, whether a coursework route has been chosen by the school. Schools publish this; most parents have never been shown it. The information sits in the centre's entry data and on the board's public syllabus page, and it determines everything a tutor should be doing.

The second job is diagnosis at the level of the mark, not the topic. A student who says she finds algebra hard is usually describing two or three specific failures: she does not change the subject of a formula reliably, she loses method marks because working is not shown, and she abandons a question when the first line does not look familiar. Those are three different repairs with three different timelines. A report that says the student needs to work on algebra names a chapter, not a fault, and gives a tutor nothing to act on in the first week.

The third job is to teach against the assessment objective rather than the textbook chapter. Each specification states how its marks are divided between knowledge, application and analysis, and each paper rewards a particular kind of answer. Learning the content is necessary and insufficient. Students in this emirate are frequently strong in recall and weak in the specific move the paper asks for, because the recall is what gets tested in school assessments and the paper move is what gets tested in May.

Lessons for families in Umm Al Quwain are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in this emirate; home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical consequence is positive: a student in Al Salamah is matched with a specialist in the exact syllabus and tier being sat, instead of whoever is prepared to drive north after a working day in Sharjah.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four stages matter to a family in this emirate: the years that build towards IGCSE, the two IGCSE years themselves, the Pearson alternative many northern-emirates schools use, and the post-16 route the grades open.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before IGCSE entries are made. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October and give a scaled score per subject rather than a grade. Schools use them to stream students and, in maths and the sciences, to decide who is pointed towards Core and who towards Extended. Weaknesses that look minor here become tier decisions two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Umm Al Quwain often move a child between schools in Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah during these years, because the commute or a fee change forces it. Each move can mean a different board, a different maths scheme and a different starting assumption about tier. Checkpoint scores are the one comparable record that travels with the student.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Two years, subject by subject, with separate syllabus codes: Mathematics 0580, Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610, First Language English 0500, Business Studies 0450, Computer Science 0478. Most subjects are tiered Core or Extended. Assessment is by written paper, with practical science assessed through a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on what the centre offers.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A student in Umm Al Quwain sitting at a Sharjah or Ajman centre follows that centre's zone, not a timetable found online.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: The other common specification in the northern emirates: Mathematics A 4MA1, Physics 4PH1, Chemistry 4CH1, Biology 4BI1, English Language A 4EA1. Grading is 9 to 1. Maths A is tiered Foundation or Higher; the separate sciences are single-tier. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical test, which changes what revision has to cover.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May/June and in November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry is a genuine option for a northern-emirates student resitting one subject while continuing with the rest of a programme.

programmes.name: What the grades open at 16
programmes.description: IGCSE grades set the entry conditions for A Level and for the IB Diploma. Most schools ask for a grade 6 or a B in the subject before allowing it at A Level, and a 7 or an A before Higher Level in the Diploma. Maths is the common block: a student who finishes at grade 5 is usually steered away from the sciences at advanced level.
programmes.countryNote: For the UAE route, Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is listed with the code a UAE centre is most likely to enter, because the code decides the papers. The description says what the specification rewards and where the marks are usually dropped rather than what the subject is about.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Cambridge splits Core across Papers 1 and 3 and Extended across Papers 2 and 4, with one non-calculator and one calculator paper at each tier. Marks go missing in the multi-step questions at the end of the calculator paper, where method marks are available but unclaimed because working is not written down.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Mathematics or Physics at advanced level. It brings differentiation, integration, binomial expansion and trigonometric identities forward into Year 11. Almost no tutor in the northern emirates teaches it, which is why families in Umm Al Quwain are usually told it is unavailable rather than taught.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Electricity and the equations of motion generate the heaviest mark losses. Cambridge candidates sit theory papers plus either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, which asks about apparatus, variables and sources of error. Pearson examines practical skills inside the written papers, so the revision has to be structured differently.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations are where the grade is decided, followed by the qualitative analysis tables that have to be recalled exactly. Organic chemistry reads as easy and marks badly, because students name products correctly and then lose the conditions, the reagent or the balancing of the equation.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · single tier at Pearson
subjects.description: The content volume is the problem, not the difficulty. Students lose marks by answering with a general description where the mark scheme wants a named structure, a named process and a direction of movement. Transport in plants, osmosis and the genetics crosses are the three reliable sources of lost marks.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Edexcel 4EA1)
subjects.description: Paper 1 tests reading, with a summary task scored for content points and for concise writing. Paper 2 tests directed writing and composition. The common failure is strong vocabulary attached to the wrong task: a student writes a pleasant description where the question asks for a speech with a stated audience and purpose.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: 0510 carries a speaking endorsement reported separately; 0511 counts speaking into the overall grade. Which one a centre enters changes how much preparation the speaking test deserves. Reading comprehension marks are lost through lifting whole sentences from the text instead of answering in the candidate's own words.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
subjects.description: Both papers reward application to the named case business and evaluation that reaches a judgement. Students write accurate definitions and stop. A six-mark answer with no reference to the case material and no decision at the end collects about half of what it could.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 covers data representation, networks and hardware; Paper 2 covers algorithms, programming and logic. Pseudocode questions lose marks on initialisation and on loop boundaries. Trace tables are marked for the intermediate values, so a correct final answer with no table earns very little.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 first language / 0544 foreign language)
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE must teach Arabic alongside the licensed international curriculum under Ministry of Education regulations. First-language and foreign-language Arabic are different specifications with different expectations, and a student placed in the wrong stream is working against a mark scheme written for somebody else.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and almost every internationally schooled student here travels out of it for school. Where a family lives changes the commute, the exam centre and the earliest hour a session can start.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: The residential concentration closest to the Sharjah road. Students from here are commonly entered at Sharjah centres, which means a Sharjah zone timetable and a school calendar set by the Sharjah Private Education Authority rather than by Umm Al Quwain's own schools.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Older housing on the peninsula, with a short run to Ajman and a longer one south. Families here often split siblings across two boards, with one child at a Cambridge centre and another at a Pearson one, so two different paper structures run in the same household.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Sits near the Ajman boundary, with the Ajman Academy run and the Sharjah run both practical. A 6pm session start is realistic on most weekdays, which makes it one of the easier parts of the emirate to timetable a weekly IGCSE hour in.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain Marina and the corniche
regions.note: Newer villa stock, a mixed resident and weekend population, and the longest average commute to a British-curriculum school. Students here usually return after 5pm, so the useful window for a full paper under timed conditions is a weekend morning rather than a weekday evening.

regions.name: Al Humrah and Al Haditha
regions.note: Industrial and old-town districts where most students attend Ministry of Education schools or Indian-curriculum schools, with IGCSE subjects sometimes taken as private candidate entries. Those candidates need their own centre and their own entry deadline, which nobody at a school is tracking for them.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Inland, roughly 40 kilometres from the coast, and the clearest case for teaching over video. An in-home tutor would spend longer driving than teaching, which is why market quotes for this part of the emirate carry a travel loading that online teaching simply does not have.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah centres on the southbound run
schoolClusters.note: Most British-curriculum students from Umm Al Quwain sit their IGCSE papers at a Sharjah centre. Fees, curricula and assessment methods in that emirate are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which is a different regulator from the one supervising schools inside Umm Al Quwain.
schools: Our Own English High School, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah

schools: RAK Academy British School Al Hamra

schoolClusters.city: Inside Umm Al Quwain
schoolClusters.note: The emirate's own private schools sit under Ministry of Education supervision, since Umm Al Quwain has no emirate-level private education authority. Programme and board details change, so confirm the current offer with each school directly before assuming a syllabus.

umm-al-quwain/igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this emirate. Each assumes live one-to-one video teaching in Gulf Standard Time, with written feedback after the session.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, one subject
modes.description: A fixed hour each week on a single syllabus code, working through the specification in the order the school is teaching it, with a short diagnostic at the start and a timed exam question at the end. This is the format that moves a grade across a term rather than across a fortnight.

Written note after each session listing what was fixed and what was set

modes.title: Paper clinic in the exam term
modes.description: From February onwards the work changes: whole papers under timed conditions, marked against the published mark scheme, then a session spent only on the questions that lost marks. Two sessions a week is common in this phase, one to sit and one to review, because marking a paper properly takes longer than sitting it.
bullets: Full past papers to time, with the mark scheme applied strictly
A written error log carried forward week to week
Separate attention to the alternative-to-practical paper where one is sat

modes.title: Two-subject split or holiday intensive
modes.description: Families carrying weaknesses in maths and one science often split a weekly hour between two subjects, or compress work into the school holidays while the commute is not eating the evening. Holiday intensives suit students who have fallen behind on content rather than on technique.
bullets: Alternating weeks, or 45 minutes on each subject
