sections.heading: Choosing a session length for the evening you actually have
paragraphs: The default tutoring product across this market is a sixty or ninety minute weekly session, and it is the wrong default for a household whose student arrives home at five. Length should be chosen from the time available and the student's state, not from a price list, and the shorter formats are not lesser versions of the long one; they do different work.

Forty-five minutes handles one objective well. One topic, one technique, one past-paper section, with the objective named at the start and checked at the end. It is the most efficient use of a tired student's attention and it is enough to move a specific weakness. What it cannot do is sustain the kind of long struggle that Higher Level problem solving or a coursework draft requires, because the valuable part of that work starts after the first twenty minutes.

Ninety minutes to two hours is for exactly that work, and in this emirate it belongs on a Saturday morning. A full timed paper followed by analysis needs that space, as does a serious pass through an internal assessment draft. Trying to do it at 6.30pm on a Wednesday after a Sharjah commute produces a tired version of a good session, which is worse value than a short session doing something achievable.

Thirty to forty minutes twice a week serves a third purpose: retention. Vocabulary, command terms, formula fluency and recall practice all respond to frequency rather than duration, and splitting an hour into two short slots usually beats keeping it whole. It also recovers better from a missed slot, which matters when the week is fragile.

sections.heading: Online, in-home and group options from this emirate
paragraphs: The comparison looks different in Umm Al Quwain than it does further south, because one of the options is largely theoretical here. In-home tutoring requires a tutor willing to drive into the emirate at the end of the working day for a single lesson, and the number of specialists prepared to sustain that is small. Families who find one often find the arrangement lapses after a few weeks for reasons nobody is at fault for.

On cost, rates published by UAE providers and rate trackers and read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 33 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, around AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, about AED 180 to AED 500 for in-home one-to-one visits once travel is accounted for, and AED 500 and above for named or examiner-marketed specialists. Monthly packages advertised include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four in-home double sessions. Those are market figures and not IB Gram prices.

A tuition centre is the other option families consider, and the problem is geography again. Centres cluster in Ajman and Sharjah, which means a second cross-border journey in the same day, taken from the part of the evening that was already short. For a student who has travelled ninety minutes home, a forty-minute drive back out is not a realistic weekly commitment regardless of what the class costs per hour.

sections.heading: Subject coverage in the least populous emirate
paragraphs: No competing page in this market will tell a parent that a subject cannot be covered locally, which is why coverage disclosure is worth more than another list of subject names. In Umm Al Quwain the position is straightforward: common IGCSE subjects are widely taught and widely tutored across the country, while narrow Higher Level Diploma courses have very few teachers nationally and essentially none resident in this emirate.

The failure mode when that is concealed is predictable. A general science graduate accepts a Diploma Chemistry booking, teaches the content competently, and has never read the internal assessment criteria closely enough to know how the evaluation marks are awarded. The family pays for real teaching and the student still loses the marks that were available, which is a worse outcome than being told to wait a week for a specialist.

Online matching makes the national pool available rather than the emirate pool, which is the whole reason it works here. A UAQ Marina student can be matched to a tutor who teaches only Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or only Cambridge 0620, across multiple exam series. Where that match is not free at the hour this household needs, the right answer is a timeline and alternative slots rather than a substitute.

sections.heading: Exam day when the centre is in another emirate
paragraphs: Exam logistics are a real problem for a commuting household and almost nobody writes about them. The student sits papers at their school, which is in Ajman, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, often starting earlier than a normal school day and sometimes with two sessions separated by hours. A journey that is tolerable on an ordinary Tuesday becomes a significant variable on a morning where arriving late means missing a paper.

There is a board-level trap on top of it. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong zone timetable was used. A family comparing dates with relatives abroad, or reading a timetable found online, can arrive on the wrong day at the right place.

The Pearson side has its own calendar to track. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are published ahead of each series and may be revised, so the school's issued version is the only one to plan from.

Practically, the things to settle in advance are the paper start times from the exams officer in writing, the journey plan for the earliest start in the series, where the student waits between two papers on a split day, and what the school's procedure is if traffic makes them late. Those four questions take one email and remove most of the risk.

sections.heading: The permit question when your tutor lives in another emirate
paragraphs: Because almost every tutor serving this emirate lives somewhere else, the permit question comes up in a slightly different form here. The answer is the same wherever the tutor sits: private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years.

The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee stated and a completion time of two working days, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts has been published.

Two related points matter for a family here. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs its own educational services permit from the relevant authority, which an individual permit does not cover. And the permit carries a code of conduct; press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Asking your child's own teacher at their Sharjah school to tutor them privately is the arrangement to avoid.

Nothing in any of this makes a regulator an endorser. No education authority accredits tutoring providers, so a claim of regulator approval should be treated as a reason to ask harder questions. The document that exists is the permit, and a legitimate tutor can show it.

sections.heading: Who supervises a school in Umm Al Quwain
paragraphs: Parents arriving from Dubai talk about inspection bands and assume a similar framework applies across the country. It does not. Umm Al Quwain's private schools sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which, in the government's own words, plays a supervisory role over private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. There is no Umm Al Quwain equivalent of Dubai's or Abu Dhabi's authority.

That matters most for a commuting household, because the school the child actually attends is probably not in this emirate. A school in Sharjah is regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education there and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A school in Ras Al Khaimah falls under the Department of Knowledge, with comparable powers. So the regulator that matters is the one covering the school, not the one covering the home.

The federal baseline applies in every case: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement, and it is why a British-curriculum school in Ajman still timetables Arabic and Islamic Education alongside IGCSE options.

For planning, the consequence is that a UAQ Marina student is carrying mandatory examined subjects on top of a full international load and a long commute. Any study plan that allocates every spare hour to IGCSE revision has not counted the whole week, and in this emirate the whole week is tighter than almost anywhere else in the country.

sections.heading: Getting started from UAQ Marina, and what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The first thing to send is not a subject but an arrival time. Tell us when your child genuinely walks through the door on a normal weekday, including bus stops, and which emirate the school is in. That single piece of information determines the session length and the slot, and getting it right at the start prevents the most common failure in this emirate, which is a plan that works for three weeks.

Then the usual specifics: the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, the level, and one recent piece of marked work. The code matters because Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers with different practical assessment arrangements, and a student practising the wrong format loses marks on presentation rather than on knowledge.

The first lesson is free and diagnostic. It works on something the student has actually been set rather than on introductions, and it ends with a short written note saying what the gap is, which format fits the evening, and how many sessions it should take. Sometimes that number is four. A provider who says four and means it is more useful than one who proposes a year and never revisits it.

On availability, the honest position for this emirate is that a narrow Higher Level specialist may not be free at the hour a UAQ Marina household needs, because that hour is late and in demand. In that case you should get a stated timeline and alternative slots rather than a substitute who nearly fits. And if a match turns out wrong after two or three sessions, the tutor is changed, because an evening this short should not be spent on a pairing that is not working.

faqs.question: Are there any IB or IGCSE tutors actually living in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: For common IGCSE subjects, possibly; for narrow Higher Level Diploma courses, almost certainly not. This is the least populous emirate with limited international school provision, so the resident population of specialist tutors in any single course is very small. The realistic alternatives are a tutor driving in from Sharjah, which tends to lapse after a few weeks, or live online one-to-one teaching matched on the syllabus rather than on geography. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; lessons are taught online, one to one, with the first one free.

faqs.question: What time can a session start if my child buses back from Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. A school bus from Sharjah city making stops often gets a UAQ Marina student home around five, which puts the earliest workable start at about 6.30pm once food and a short gap are allowed for. From Ajman the same calculation gives roughly 5.30pm, and a private car rather than a bus moves both earlier. Work from the actual arrival time including stops, not from the final bell, because the difference between the two is where plans in this emirate usually fail.

faqs.question: Is forty-five minutes long enough to be worth booking?
faqs.answer: For one objective, yes, and for a student who has just travelled ninety minutes it is often better than an hour. Forty-five minutes handles one topic, one technique or one past-paper section with the objective named at the start and checked at the end. What it cannot do is sustain the long struggle that Higher Level problem solving or a coursework draft needs, because the valuable part of that work begins after the first twenty minutes. Put that work on a Saturday morning instead.

faqs.question: Why should a long session go on the weekend rather than a weekday?
faqs.answer: Because the quality of the hour differs. A rested student on a Saturday morning with no commute behind them can attempt a hard problem, fail at it usefully, and then have it fixed properly, which is exactly how Higher Level technique and coursework drafting work. The same ninety minutes at 6.30pm on a Wednesday after a cross-emirate journey produces a tired version of a good session. One weekend block often replaces two weekday sessions rather than adding to them.

faqs.question: Would a tuition centre in Ajman or Sharjah be more practical?
faqs.answer: Rarely on a weekday, because it means a second cross-border journey in the same day, taken out of an evening that was already short. For a student who has travelled ninety minutes home, a forty-minute drive back out is not a weekly commitment most households can sustain regardless of the per-hour cost. A centre can make sense in school holidays, when the journey is not competing with homework and fatigue, or for a student whose school is near the centre anyway.

faqs.question: How much do tutors charge for families in this part of the UAE?
faqs.answer: Rates published by UAE providers and rate trackers, read in October 2026, run roughly from AED 33 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for in-home visits once travel is priced in, and AED 500 and above for named or examiner-marketed specialists. Monthly packages advertised include about AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices; ask us directly for a current quote.

faqs.question: Our school is in Sharjah. Which regulator actually governs it?
faqs.answer: The Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in that emirate and also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Umm Al Quwain's own private schools are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which performs that role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. For a commuting household the regulator that matters is the one covering the school, not the one covering the home, and the two are usually different here.

faqs.question: Does my tutor need a permit if they live in a different emirate?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit is federal, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, so it applies wherever in the UAE the tutor is based. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE lists a two working day completion time for the service. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see the permit; no education regulator accredits tutoring providers, so claims of regulator approval should prompt harder questions.

faqs.question: Can my child's own teacher at their Sharjah school tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: That is the one arrangement to avoid. The private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct, and press reporting on Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules describes school staff being barred from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules there is an obvious conflict in paying the person who marks the work. A specialist with no connection to the school can be matched on the syllabus instead, which also avoids any awkwardness if the arrangement needs to end.

faqs.question: What do we need to plan for exam day when the centre is in another emirate?
faqs.answer: Four things, settled by one email to the exams officer. The correct zone timetable version, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. The paper start times in writing, since some start earlier than a normal school day. Where the student waits between two papers on a split day. And the school's procedure if traffic delays them. Those four remove most of the risk.

faqs.question: When do November Pearson Edexcel results arrive?
faqs.answer: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. The January date is the one that matters if a November entry is being used as a retake, because it decides whether a result exists in time for an application deadline. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and they can be revised, so plan from the version the school issues.

faqs.question: How should the plan change during Ramadan with this commute?
faqs.answer: Move everything after Iftar and shorten it. The school day is shorter, so the commute is often easier, but afternoons are the least productive hours for a fasting student and the evening is where real work happens. A forty-five minute post-Iftar session around 8.30pm holds better than anything attempted in the afternoon. It also helps to move new abstract content out of the period and use it for consolidation and past-paper review, then rebuild the normal pattern afterwards.

Vocabulary, command terms, formula fluency and recall practice all respond to frequency rather than duration, so two thirty or forty-minute slots usually outperform a single hour on the same material. The split also fits a commuting week better, because the gaps this emirate leaves are short rather than absent, and it recovers more easily from a missed slot. Keep the hour whole for problem solving and coursework, where the student needs time to get into a hard question.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free at the only time we can do?
faqs.answer: You should be told so, given a timeline, and offered alternative slots, rather than matched with the nearest available substitute. The late evening slots this emirate needs are the ones most in demand nationally, so for a narrow Higher Level subject the wait can be a week or more. That is a worse answer than instant availability and a better outcome than paying a competent generalist who has never read the internal assessment criteria for the course your child is taking.

faqs.question: Does living in a small emirate mean fewer subject options at school?
faqs.answer: In practice yes, which is why most secondary-age students here travel out of the emirate for an international curriculum. Narrower option blocks mean a student may end up with a subject combination produced by the timetable rather than chosen, and smaller Diploma cohorts mean fewer Higher Level options and fewer classmates taking the same course. When comparing schools in Ajman, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, compare the actual subject lists each one can offer your child in their year group rather than the programme names.

umm-al-quwain/uaq-marina.closingHeading: Send your real arrival time and we will build the plan around it
umm-al-quwain/uaq-marina.closingBody: The most useful first message from UAQ Marina has one unusual thing in it: the time your child actually walks through the door on a normal weekday, including bus stops, and which emirate the school is in. Add the subject, the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, and one recent piece of marked work. The first lesson is free, taught online one to one over live video, and it ends with a written note on the gap, the session format that fits your evening, and how many sessions it should take. If nobody is free at your slot, you will be told the timeline instead.

intro.heading: The weekend is the only block of IB time a UAE family actually controls
paragraphs: Most UAE private schools run Monday to Friday, which puts the school weekend on Saturday and Sunday. For a Diploma student that matters more than it sounds. Monday to Thursday is school until mid-afternoon, then a CAS commitment, then a fixture, then an hour of homework that is already late. A 4:30pm session on a Tuesday is taught to a tired child who has been concentrating since 7:30am. Saturday morning is a different animal: the student is rested, nothing else is booked, and two consecutive hours exist without anyone negotiating for them. That is why a weekend IB tutor in the UAE is usually the first scheduling decision a family gets right.

The second decision is what those hours are for. A weekend session that drifts into whatever the student happens to be worried about produces a pleasant conversation and no marks. The Diploma runs on a fixed calendar: internal deadlines for the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the TOK essay, a mock window, predicted grades, and then the May session UAE schools sit. Each of those has a date attached, set either by the school or by the board. Counting weekends backwards from those dates is what turns a Saturday into a plan rather than a habit, and it is the organising idea behind this whole page.

So this page is built as a calendar rather than a brochure. It counts the weekends backwards from the exam window and says what each one is for. It quotes the Cambridge and Pearson deadlines that those boards publish themselves, and it is honest about the IB dates that are not confirmed here. It publishes IB tutor rates in AED per hour, because three of the six pages currently ranking for these searches publish no price at all. It also sets out what a tutor may and may not touch on a piece of assessed work, which is the question UAE parents ask least often and need most.

IB Gram matches UAE families to IB specialists and delivers every lesson one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. There is no IB Gram premises anywhere in the UAE and no tutor is sent to a UAE address; home visiting is a service offered only in India. For a Higher Level subject that is an advantage rather than a compromise. A family in Mirdif gets a Chemistry HL specialist who may sit in Abu Dhabi, Muscat or Mumbai, instead of whichever tutor happens to be willing to drive to Mirdif for 9am on a Saturday morning.

What follows assumes you are deciding something concrete: which day, how long, how many weeks, and what you should have in your hand at the end of each one. The first lesson is free and needs no card details, so the cheapest way to test any of this is to book a single Saturday and judge the written note that lands afterwards. If the note names a topic, a mark scheme and a task for the coming week, the slot is worth keeping. If it says the session went well, it is not worth keeping, whoever the tutor is.

weekend-ib-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB is four programmes, and a weekend plan looks completely different in each. A PYP Saturday is forty minutes on reading fluency and number facts. A DP2 Saturday is two hours on Paper 3 technique with a mark scheme open on screen. Here is what each programme asks of a weekend, and what a UAE family running it should expect those hours to carry.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: PYP is inquiry-led and reports against learner profile attributes rather than percentages, which makes it hard for a parent to see a gap until it is wide. Weekend work at this stage is short and frequent: thirty to forty-five minutes on reading fluency, number bonds, written sentence structure or a unit of inquiry the child has lost the thread of. Two short Saturday sessions beat one long one, because attention at eight years old is the binding constraint, not content.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools, PYP children also carry Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies from the early years, so the weekend already has demands on it before a tutor is involved. Families here usually book one short English or maths block on Saturday morning and keep Sunday clear, because the Arabic homework tends to land for Monday.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP marks against four criteria per subject on a one-to-eight scale, and the weakest criterion is almost always the one nobody has looked at. Weekend sessions here are diagnostic: read the criterion descriptors with the student, find out which strand the marks are leaking from, and practise that strand against the actual task. MYP5 adds the Personal Project, which has a process journal that cannot be reconstructed the weekend before it is due.
programmes.countryNote: A good number of UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE for Years 10 and 11, so a UAE MYP student may be preparing for Cambridge or Pearson papers rather than MYP eAssessment. The weekend plan has to know which, because the entry deadlines and the command terms are not the same.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where weekend tutoring earns its money, because the load is not just six subjects but six Internal Assessments plus the Extended Essay and the TOK essay, all with internal school deadlines stacked between September and March. Weekend blocks are long enough to do real work on one of those and still leave time for timed paper practice. The sequencing matters more than the hours: coursework first, then papers, never both in one session.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and the November session exists for a small number of candidates and retakes. No IB exam or results date is published on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date on a planning page is worse than no date. Confirm every IB deadline with your school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP pairs two or more DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language portfolio. Weekend support here is unusual in shape: the DP courses need ordinary subject teaching, while the reflective project needs process coaching and a realistic schedule. Students often underestimate the reflective project because it has no exam attached, and then lose a term to it.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools compared with the DP, so a CP student frequently cannot find a local tutor who has taught the course at all. This is the clearest case for online delivery: the subject specialist and the CP-experienced mentor are rarely the same person and almost never in the same emirate.

weekend-ib-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families most often book weekend help for, with what each one actually assesses and where the marks tend to disappear. Higher and Standard Level are treated separately, because the papers differ and so does the Internal Assessment weighting. If a subject is not on the grid, ask anyway: the specialist pool is wider than a list of ten.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The HL course adds proof, complex numbers and deeper calculus, and HL candidates sit a third paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. Weekend sessions are where a student can sit a full Paper 3 under the clock, which no weekday evening allows. Marks usually go on unjustified steps, not wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: AI is modelling and statistics led, with heavy graphical calculator use, and students who choose it to avoid algebra are regularly caught out by the statistics. The exploration here lives or dies on whether the data set is real and the question is answerable. A Saturday block is the only realistic time to collect and clean data.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics punishes unit errors, significant figures and sloppy definitions more than it punishes conceptual gaps. HL adds further material and a heavier Paper 2. Weekend work tends to split into one block on a topic the student has written off, usually fields or thermodynamics, and one on examiner-style wording.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are the two topics UAE families call about most, and both reward repeated short practice over single long explanations. The HL extension is substantial. Internal Assessment work in Chemistry needs uncertainty handling discussed properly, which is a weekend-length conversation rather than a twenty-minute one.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology looks like a memory subject and is assessed as a data subject. Students lose marks on command terms, graph interpretation and the difference between describing and explaining a trend. Weekend sessions that work are built around past-paper data questions with the mark scheme open, not around re-reading notes.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The portfolio of commentaries on published news articles is the component students leave latest and regret most. Each commentary is short, which makes it deceptively easy. HL adds quantitative content and a third paper. Weekend sessions are well used on article selection, because a bad article cannot be rescued by good analysis.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The written assignment and the case study reward structure and tool selection, not volume. Students who write everything they know about a firm score below students who answer the question with one framework applied properly. A weekend block is enough to plan and redraft a single response from scratch.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Paper 1 unseen analysis are both performance tasks, and both improve with rehearsal rather than reading. Weekend sessions suit this: there is time to attempt a full fifteen-minute oral, hear it back, and attempt it again, which a weekday half-hour cannot accommodate.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The solution development component needs a working artefact and documented evidence of a real client interaction, both of which collapse if started late. HL adds abstract data structures and a case study that changes annually. Weekend sessions are the only block long enough to debug and document in one sitting.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic sits in Group 2 for most international-school students in the UAE, and it also appears as a KHDA-mandated subject in its own right. The two are not the same course. Weekend speaking practice is the component families neglect, and it is the one that needs a live human rather than an app.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Neither has an exam, so both slide, and both are capable of costing a bilingual diploma point. TOK runs on prescribed titles and the EE on a research question that has to be narrow enough to finish. Weekend sessions here are process coaching on the student's own work, with the school's supervisor retaining sign-off.

subjects.name: Geography and Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: Both reward case-study specificity, and both are taught by generalists in smaller UAE schools. Students arrive with four named case studies and need ten. A weekend block spent building a case-study bank with figures attached is worth more than three sessions of content revision.

weekend-ib-tutor.regionsTitle: What a weekend looks like in each emirate
weekend-ib-tutor.regionsIntro: Weekend tutoring is a logistics problem before it is an academic one, and the logistics change by emirate. School weeks, regulators, holiday calendars and road time all differ. Below is what the weekend looks like in each of the seven emirates and in Al Ain, and what that means for the hour you are about to book.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Two hundred and twenty-seven private schools answer to KHDA, running seventeen curricula between them, and Saturday morning is the most contested tutoring hour in the country. Families in Arabian Ranches, Mirdif and Jumeirah book an 8am or 9am weekend IB tutor in Dubai in September and hold the slot all year.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. A weekend IB tutor in Abu Dhabi is therefore someone from outside the school, which is also the sounder arrangement academically.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK alongside Abu Dhabi but has far fewer IB World Schools, so Higher Level specialists in Physics, Chemistry and Maths AA are genuinely thin locally. Online delivery is what makes a Saturday HL session possible here at all, rather than a compromise on who teaches it.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah parents work in Dubai, so Friday evening and Sunday afternoon are often easier to protect than Saturday morning in these households.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Ajman's private schools are supervised federally by the Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority. IB provision is limited here, and most Ajman students we support sit IGCSE or Ministry tracks, sometimes adding one or two IB subjects later through another school.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain also sits with the federal Ministry of Education. It appears in none of the competitor pages researched for this project, and local specialist supply is close to zero, which makes a standing online weekend slot the only arrangement that survives a full term.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Weekend road time to Dubai runs to an hour and a half each way, so a travelling tutor consumes most of a Saturday before any teaching begins.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools are supervised by the Ministry of Education. The east-coast drive makes a travelling tutor expensive in both money and hours, and the weekend is usually the only window a Fujairah Diploma student has that the school commute does not already own.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai
schoolClusters.note: Dubai's IB cluster is large enough that weekend demand is subject-specific rather than general: Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL and Economics HL fill first. Students from these schools typically want a slot that sits either side of a Saturday sports fixture, which is why two-hour morning blocks and 6pm Sunday sessions are the two shapes that actually hold.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi's IB families contend with ADEK's ethics rules on one side and a smaller specialist pool on the other, so the weekend tutor is almost always from outside the emirate. Al Ain students in particular book earlier in the year, because the Higher Level science slots are gone by October.

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: The northern emirates mix IB, Cambridge, Pearson and Ministry tracks within a short radius, so a family may have one child on MYP criteria and another on a Pearson entry deadline. Weekend scheduling here is usually built around a parent's Dubai commute rather than around the school day.

weekend-ib-tutor.modesIntro: Four weekend shapes cover almost every family who asks. The right one depends on the year group and on how close the session sits to a deadline, not on preference. All four are delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all four are open to change at the half-term review.

modes.title: The Saturday two-hour deep block
modes.description: The default for DP1 and DP2. Two hours is long enough to teach a method, practise it under timed conditions, and compare the attempt against a mark scheme in one sitting, which is the full loop. An hour is long enough for the first two steps only, and the third step is where the marks are. Saturday morning rather than afternoon, because the student is rested and nothing has yet been rescheduled on top of it.

It works best for MYP students and for DP students in a coursework-heavy stretch: the session plans what will be done Monday to Thursday, breaks the next deadline into three weekday tasks, and leaves the student with something written. Families running two children often take Saturday for one and Sunday for the other.

The logic is that during the day the student is already in school revision programmes, and adding a weekday evening produces diminishing returns. The weekend blocks become the place where full papers are sat and marked rather than where content is re-covered.

It also survives travel better, because a 7pm Gulf Standard Time slot is still workable from most of the time zones UAE families travel into.

sections.heading: What a weekend IB tutor actually means in a Monday-to-Friday UAE week
paragraphs: A weekend IB tutor in the UAE is a subject specialist who teaches your child on Saturday or Sunday, when the school week has released them. Because UAE private schools run Monday to Friday, the weekend is Saturday and Sunday, and those two days are the only part of the week a family schedules rather than inherits. Everything else is school, prayer, commitments and travel. Booking there is not a convenience choice; it is the difference between a planned hour and a borrowed one.

The practical argument for the weekend is cognitive rather than logistical. A Diploma student who has been in class since 7:30am has already spent their best concentration. Teaching a new method into that state produces recognition without retention: the student follows the explanation, agrees with it, and cannot reproduce it on Thursday. Saturday morning sessions are taught to a student who can hold a chain of reasoning for ninety minutes. The same tutor, the same topic and the same price produce a different result at 9am on Saturday than at 5pm on Tuesday.

The argument against the weekend is real and worth stating. Teenagers need unstructured time, and a Diploma student with six subjects and a CAS programme needs it more than most. The honest position is that one weekend block, protected and purposeful, costs less of a child's weekend than three scattered weekday sessions that each eat an evening. A single two-hour Saturday morning leaves the whole of Saturday afternoon and all of Sunday intact. That is the trade this page is arguing for, and it only works if the two hours are planned.

Weekend IB tuition at IB Gram is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time so neither party is working at an awkward hour. No tutor attends a UAE address: that service exists only in India. What it buys instead is the subject specialist your child's syllabus actually needs rather than the nearest available person, which is the whole reason online delivery wins in a market where Higher Level supply is concentrated in two emirates.

sections.heading: The weekend ledger: counting Saturdays backwards from the May session
paragraphs: A Diploma year has roughly thirty-six usable weekends in it, and about eight of those disappear into holidays, travel and exam weeks. That leaves under thirty. Written down like that, the planning question answers itself: you cannot do everything, so each weekend needs one job. Counting backwards from the exam window rather than forwards from September is what makes the allocation visible, and it is what no competitor page in this market does.

The table below is the ledger in its general form. It is not tied to a specific IB date, because no IB session or results date is confirmed on this page. It is tied to the shape every Diploma year has: coursework front-loaded between September and March, a mock window in the middle, predicted grades formed off the mocks, then a run of timed practice into study leave. Your school's internal deadlines sit inside that shape, and your IB coordinator holds the exact dates.

Read the last column first. Each weekend should end with something a parent can see: a proposal, a marked paper, a list of dropped topics, a submitted piece of coursework. If a block ends with nothing that leaves the room, the block was a conversation. That is the single most useful test available to a UAE parent paying weekend rates, and it needs no knowledge of the subject at all.

The ledger also answers the question families ask in February: is it too late? Starting with ten weekends left is a different plan from starting with thirty, not a worse one. With ten, coursework is finished or abandoned, and every remaining block goes to whole papers and self-marking. The plan changes; the method of counting does not.

sections.heading: The board deadlines that land midweek and get prepared at the weekend
paragraphs: Entry deadlines are administrative, they fall on weekdays, and they are missed by families who assumed the school had it covered. The work of checking them happens at the weekend, because that is when a parent and a student are in the same room with the subject list. Cambridge and Pearson both publish their key dates, and the pattern they show is the thing worth internalising: entries close months before the papers are sat.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. There is a detail in Cambridge's own exams officers' guide that catches UAE centres specifically: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your school which zone it sits in, and check the timetable version against it.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May or June and in November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which means dates can still be revised. The practical consequence is that no page should be a family's source of truth for a date. Use the table below to understand the shape and the lead times, then open the official timetable on the board's own site before you write anything in a calendar.

For the IB itself this page publishes no date at all. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so nothing could be verified from the IB directly, and an unverified exam date on a planning page is actively harmful. UAE schools sit the May session; the November session exists for a smaller group of candidates. Every IB deadline your weekend plan depends on should come from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org itself.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the weekends the UAE calendar quietly removes
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has breaks that no generic revision timetable accounts for, and two of them sit in the worst possible places. A plan written in September that assumes thirty available weekends will be wrong by February, and the correction always comes at the expense of the last clear run before exams. Building the Ramadan weekend schedule into the plan in January costs nothing; discovering it in March costs the plan.

Ramadan shortens school days in most UAE private schools, and it changes when a teenager can concentrate. A 10am Saturday block during Ramadan is being taught to a fasting student at the hardest point of the day. The straightforward fix is to move weekend sessions to the evening after Iftar, or to consolidate two short blocks into one longer Sunday session. Tutors working with UAE families should be offering that before being asked; it is the single most common reason a Ramadan term loses momentum.

The holiday weekends matter in a second way, which is sequencing. Spring break often falls immediately before study leave in an exam year, which means the most valuable revision weekends of the entire Diploma sit inside a family holiday. That is not an argument against the holiday. It is an argument for booking those specific weekends in January, so the family knows in advance whether they are revision weekends or holiday weekends and the plan is built on the honest answer.

The table sets out each period, what it does to a weekend block, and the absorption that actually works. None of this is exotic; it is the kind of operational detail that is absent from every competitor page researched for this market, where the calendar is treated as though it were European.

sections.heading: What a two-hour Saturday block should actually contain
paragraphs: Parents paying weekend rates are entitled to know what the two hours are made of, and most providers will not tell them. The structure below is not a style preference; it follows from how marks are lost. A session that explains well and practises little produces a student who understands the topic and still drops the marks, because the marks come from timing, notation and command terms rather than from comprehension.

The order matters more than the content. Modelling has to come before practice, or the practice rehearses the student's existing error until it is faster. Timing has to come before mark-scheme work, or the student marks an untimed attempt that bears no relation to what happens in the hall. And the week's task has to be set inside the session and written down, because a weekend block with no weekday follow-through is a weekly reset rather than a programme.

The ten-minute opening is the part tutors most often skip and the part that decides the session. A tutor who has planned the two hours before hearing what went wrong in school this week has planned the wrong two hours. Five honest minutes from the student about Thursday's test or Wednesday's lesson usually relocates the whole block, and a tutor who cannot change plan on that information is working from a script.

The break is in the table deliberately. Two hours without one costs the second hour, and a tutor who refuses a five-minute break to maximise contact time is selling minutes rather than marks. Everything in the final column is something that leaves the session: a method in the student's own notation, a count of marks attempted under the clock, a list of where those marks went, a task the parent can see by Wednesday.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and whether Saturday costs more
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are IB tutor rates in AED per hour as providers in this market publish them, with the provider named against each figure and the month the figure was read. These are market rates rather than IB Gram's, and they are published so that a quote you receive can be placed in a band rather than accepted blind.

The weekend premium is real but it is not usually a published rate. It shows up as position within the band: Saturday morning slots with a scarce Higher Level specialist get quoted at the top of the range because they are the first to go, while Sunday evening and Friday evening sit lower. For in-home visits the weekend effect is structural rather than commercial, because travel time is inside the hourly rate and weekend road time between emirates is less predictable than a weekday evening run.

Two cost-in-context points are worth holding alongside the table. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. And Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Tutoring demand is growing against a frozen fee base, which is part of why weekend specialist slots tighten in September.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page. The honest reason is that the rate depends on subject, level and how close the session sits to a deadline, and a single number would be wrong for most readers. The first lesson is free and needs no card details, and the quote comes after that lesson, against a named tutor and a written plan rather than against a band.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or group: the weekend version of the choice
paragraphs: The weekend changes this comparison in ways a weekday version does not capture. Road time is less predictable, tuition centres run fixed timetables that cannot be moved around a fixture, and school-run revision sessions follow the school's calendar rather than the family's. Meanwhile the thing that is genuinely scarce in this market, a Higher Level specialist in a shortage subject, is scarce everywhere at once on a Saturday morning.

IB Gram's position is one-to-one online over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor attends a UAE address; that service runs only in India. The case for it is not that travel is inconvenient. The case is that it decouples who teaches your child from who lives within driving distance, which in a country where IB Higher Level provision concentrates in Dubai and Abu Dhabi is the entire ballgame for a family in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain.

The honest limitations belong here too. Younger PYP children often do need an adult physically at the table, and for them a short online session works only with a parent nearby for the first few weeks. Science practical skills can be taught and analysed online but the apparatus work happens at school. And a student who will not switch their camera on is not being tutored, whatever the format; that is a conversation to have in week one rather than week six.

The last row of the table is the one families underrate. Self-study with past papers and a mark scheme is free, available every weekend, and the first thing to slip. A good weekend tutor spends part of the term making themselves less necessary by teaching a student to mark their own work honestly. If that is not happening by the third month, the arrangement has become a subscription.

sections.heading: What a weekend tutor may and may not do with IA, EE and TOK work
paragraphs: This is the question UAE parents ask least and need most, and it is the one place where getting it wrong costs a student their diploma rather than a few marks. Coursework tends to be done at the weekend, which means the weekend tutor is the person most likely to be asked to cross a line. The boundary should be agreed in writing before the first session, not negotiated at 10pm the night before an internal deadline.

The rule is simple to state. A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not supply text, data, code or mathematics that then appears in a submission. Everything in the second column of the table is legitimate teaching and much of it is exactly what a good supervisor would do. Everything in the third column is academic misconduct, regardless of who suggested it, and the student carries the consequence.

There is a commercial dimension worth naming. One provider researched for this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price. That is not a grey area and it is not a competitive disadvantage for us to refuse it; it is an IB malpractice trigger that can end a candidature. A UAE family comparing weekend providers should ask the direct question, and should treat a vague answer as the answer.

The fourth column exists because sign-off never belongs to a tutor. The subject teacher, the EE supervisor and the TOK teacher assess against the published criteria and record authenticity. A weekend tutor who claims to know what a piece of work will score is guessing, and a weekend tutor who offers to handle the school's process for you is describing something that is not theirs to handle.

sections.heading: The criterion letters behind a Mathematics exploration, and what a weekend review checks
paragraphs: No competitor page researched for this market names a single Internal Assessment criterion, which is remarkable given that a fifth of a Mathematics grade sits in one. Students lose marks there in predictable, diagnosable ways, and a weekend review session that works through the criteria by letter is one of the highest-value two hours available in the whole Diploma. Content teaching cannot recover those marks later; nothing else in the course assesses them.

The pattern is consistent. Students over-invest in the mathematics and under-invest in presentation, personal engagement and reflection, because those sound like soft criteria and are not. Reflection in particular is where strong mathematicians drop marks: they do the work, get the answer, and never discuss what the limitation of their model was or what they would do differently. A reviewer reading for that criterion finds nothing to reward.

Use the table as a checklist rather than as a specification. Criterion names and mark allocations are set by the current subject guide, which the school holds, and guides are revised. Confirm the exact wording and the current allocation with your child's teacher or IB coordinator before you plan around it. What does not change is the method: read each criterion, find the paragraph in the draft that is meant to earn it, and if there is no such paragraph, that is the finding.

A weekend review session is also the right place to be realistic about scope. The most common reason an exploration underperforms is that the question was too large to answer properly in the word allowance, and that decision was made in September. Catching it in October costs one session. Catching it in February costs the mark.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and the mandatory UAE subjects sharing the weekend
paragraphs: Which authority licenses your child's school changes what a weekend plan has to work around, and it is worth knowing which one you are dealing with. In Dubai, KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That is the complete map, and ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project.

Two of those bodies go further than inspection. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not just quality assurance sits with the emirate. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is the reason your child carries UAE subjects alongside the IB.

In Dubai this is specific and documented. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

For a weekend plan, the consequence is practical. These subjects generate homework and assessments that compete for exactly the hours a tutoring block wants, and families routinely discover in February that the Arabic grade is the one holding a report back. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. Support there is therefore about the student's own school material, not a parallel syllabus.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the paperwork that needs a weekend of its own
paragraphs: Equivalency is the step UAE families discover late. An IB or IGCSE certificate earned at a UAE school still needs to be recognised by the Ministry of Education for use in UAE higher education and employment, and the requirements are subject-specific rather than general. None of the competitor pages researched for four of ten query clusters mention equivalency at all, and one ranking page publishes the wrong subject count, which is a useful illustration of why this should be read from the source.

For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That last point is the one a competitor got wrong, and it matters because it changes which subjects a Year 11 student should be entered for.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB specifically, no points threshold is published on this page, because none was read on the Ministry's own site. Anyone quoting an IB equivalency figure should be asked where they read it.

Equivalency is a process IB Gram describes and does not perform. No tutor can expedite it, guarantee it or submit it on your behalf, and tutoring is not required for it. What a weekend session can usefully do is sit down with the subject list in front of you in October of Year 11 or DP1, check it against the published requirement, and identify the gap while there is still an entry window open. That is an hour, once, and it is the cheapest hour on this page.

sections.heading: Getting a Saturday slot when every UAE family wants the same hour
paragraphs: Weekend supply is the real constraint in this market and almost nobody discloses it. Saturday between 9am and midday is the single most requested window in the country, and the tutors who go first are the Higher Level specialists in the shortage subjects: Maths AA HL, Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Economics HL. By late October those specific slots are generally taken for the year, which is why the families who get what they want booked in September.

When a weekend slot with the right specialist is not available, there are four honest answers and one dishonest one. The honest answers are: wait for a slot and start midweek in the meantime; take a Sunday or Friday evening slot instead; take a shorter weekly block with the specialist rather than a longer one with a generalist; or take a tutor outside UAE hours whose availability maps onto a Gulf Standard Time weekend morning. The dishonest answer is to put a generalist in the chair and call them a specialist.

IB Gram's tutor pool includes UAE-based specialists and specialists elsewhere, including India, and which one your child gets depends on subject, level and the hour you need. That is disclosed rather than concealed; several providers in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE numbers without saying so. You will know who is teaching your child, where they are teaching from, and what they have taught before the first lesson, not after it.

The sequence that works is short. Tell us the subject, the level, the school and the two weekend hours that are genuinely free. We come back with named availability inside those hours, or we say plainly that it does not exist this term and what the nearest workable alternative is. Then one free lesson, no card details, and a written note you can judge. If the note is thin, the match is wrong, and a different tutor is a sentence away.

process.title: Tell us the weekend hours you genuinely have
process.description: Not the hours you wish you had. Send the subject, the level, the school, the board where it is not the IB, and the two weekend windows that are actually free after fixtures, family commitments and travel. A plan built on optimistic availability collapses in week three, and rebuilding it costs more than being honest at the start.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a Saturday or Sunday
process.description: One lesson, no charge, no card details taken. It runs in the slot you intend to keep, with the tutor you would keep, on a topic from your child's current school work rather than a prepared demonstration. Afterwards you get a written note. That note is the thing to judge, because it is what you will receive every week.

process.title: The backwards plan, written down
process.description: Before the second session, the tutor produces a plan counted backwards from the exam window: which weekend carries which job, where the school's internal coursework deadlines fall, which weekends the UAE calendar removes, and what should exist at the end of each block. It is one page. If it cannot fit on one page it has not been thought through.

process.title: Weekend sessions with a written note each time
process.description: Every block ends with a short note naming the topic covered, the marks lost and why, and the task set for the coming week. Across a term those notes become a record of whether the arrangement is working, which is far more useful than a monthly phone call about how your child is doing in general terms.

process.title: A half-term review, including the option to stop
process.description: At each half-term we look at the notes together and decide what changes: a different shape, a different day, a second subject, fewer hours, or none. Stopping when the gap has closed is a legitimate outcome and we will say so. A weekend slot that has become a subscription is not serving your child or the next family waiting for it.

whyPoints.title: The weekend is planned, not filled
whyPoints.description: Every block is allocated against a deadline on the written plan, counted backwards from the exam window. Nobody arrives at a Saturday session and asks what the student would like to look at today. That question is how two hours become a conversation, and it is the most common failure mode in weekend tutoring at any price.

whyPoints.title: Gulf Standard Time, not a European working day
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, which sounds obvious and is not. Several providers ranking for these searches quote in pounds or dollars and run on UK hours, so a UAE Saturday morning slot is somebody's night shift. Timezone-shifted tutors cancel more, reschedule more and know less about the UAE school calendar.

whyPoints.title: Specialist by subject and level, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Delivery is one-to-one over live video, which means the pool is every specialist available at your hour rather than everyone within driving distance of your community. For Higher Level Chemistry, Physics or Maths AA in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

whyPoints.title: Coursework boundaries in writing, first
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may and may not do with an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay is agreed in writing before the first session. The tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work, and sign-off stays with the school. In a market where one provider sells finished coursework, this is worth putting in writing.

whyPoints.title: Sourced numbers, or no number
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page carry the provider that published them and the month they were read. Regulatory statements carry the authority that issued them. No IB exam date is published here because none could be verified from the IB directly. A planning page that invents a date is worse than a planning page that says it does not know.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated honestly
whyPoints.description: If no weekend slot exists this term with the specialist your child needs, you will be told that and offered the nearest real alternative. No competitor page researched for this market discloses a coverage limit at all. Knowing what is not available is what lets a family plan around it rather than discover it in February.

faqs.question: Is a weekend IB tutor better than a session after school during the week?
faqs.answer: For most Diploma students, yes, and the reason is attention rather than convenience. A student taught at 4:30pm on a Tuesday has been concentrating since 7:30am and will follow an explanation without retaining it. Saturday morning gives you a rested student and two uninterrupted hours, which is long enough to teach a method, practise it under timed conditions and compare the attempt with a mark scheme. That full loop is where marks come from. Weekday sessions still work well for short set-up conversations and for younger students, but for Higher Level content the weekend block is the one that changes results.

faqs.question: Our school week runs Monday to Friday. Which day actually works better, Saturday or Sunday?
faqs.answer: Saturday morning for teaching, Sunday for planning. Saturday gives you the longest clear stretch and the freshest student, so it suits a two-hour block with new content and timed practice. Sunday sits immediately before the school week, which makes it the better day for mapping the coming week's deadlines and setting tasks the student will actually do on Monday. Families with two children frequently split the days rather than stacking both on Saturday. The one combination to avoid is a late Sunday evening session with new material, because nothing taught then survives Monday morning.

faqs.question: Do weekend lessons cost more per hour in the UAE than weekday ones?
faqs.answer: Rarely as a published premium, but usually as position within the band. Market rates for a qualified subject tutor online run roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, and Saturday morning slots with a scarce Higher Level specialist get quoted at the top of that range because they go first. In-home visits are different: travel time sits inside the hourly rate, and weekend road time between emirates is less predictable than a weekday evening, so distance pushes the quote up. Ask whether the rate differs by day before booking.

faqs.question: How many weekends are actually left before the May session, and how do we count them?
faqs.answer: Count calendar weekends to the start of the exam window, then subtract the ones the UAE calendar removes: the December break, Eid Al Fitr, spring break, and any travel you already know about. A Diploma year has roughly thirty-six weekends and loses about eight, which leaves under thirty for everything including coursework, mocks and timed practice. Written down, that number makes the planning decisions for you. It also answers the February question honestly: starting with ten weekends left is a different plan, not a hopeless one, because coursework is settled and every block goes to whole papers.

faqs.question: After two Saturday sessions we have nothing to show. What should each weekend produce?
faqs.answer: Something that leaves the room. A proposal with a method and a variable, a marked past paper with the lost marks grouped by command term, a written list of topics being dropped and kept, or a task the student can be seen doing on Wednesday. The test does not require any subject knowledge: ask what exists now that did not exist on Friday. If the answer is that the session went well and your child understands it better, two hours at weekend rates bought a conversation. Raise it at once rather than at half-term, and ask for the written note to change shape.

faqs.question: Can a weekend tutor help with the Internal Assessment without crossing IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear enough to put in writing before the first session. A tutor may test whether a research question is answerable with the data available, teach the mathematics or method it needs, review a draft the student has produced and give feedback against the published criteria. A tutor may not supply finished text, data or mathematics that then appears in the submission, and may not edit a piece to completion. Sign-off always stays with the school's subject teacher or supervisor. Any provider offering to hand over a finished Internal Assessment is describing something that can end a candidature.

faqs.question: During Ramadan, can our weekend sessions move to after Iftar?
faqs.answer: Yes, and a tutor working with UAE families should offer it before being asked. Ramadan shortens school days in most private schools and changes when a teenager can concentrate, so a 10am Saturday block is being taught at the hardest point of a fasting day. The usual adjustments are to move to a post-Iftar evening slot, or to consolidate two short weekend blocks into one longer Sunday session. Build it into the plan in January rather than renegotiating in the first week of Ramadan, because the weeks either side of Eid Al Fitr need the lost hours redistributed in advance.

faqs.question: We travel most long weekends. Can a weekend schedule follow us abroad?
faqs.answer: That is one of the clearer advantages of online delivery. Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time and a 7pm slot remains workable from most of the destinations UAE families travel to, so the slot survives the trip. For travel-heavy terms a Friday evening session often holds better than a Saturday morning one, because departures tend to be Friday night or Saturday. What matters is deciding in advance which weekends are study weekends and which are not, rather than cancelling in the same week and losing the hour altogether.

faqs.question: Is one two-hour Saturday block better than two one-hour sessions in the week?
faqs.answer: For Diploma content, usually yes. One hour is long enough to teach a method and start practising it, which means the mark-scheme comparison gets pushed to homework and generally does not happen. Two hours completes the loop inside the session, with a short break in the middle because two hours without one costs the second hour. For younger PYP children the reverse holds: two short sessions beat one long one, because attention is the binding constraint at that age rather than content. MYP students sit in between and often do best with one block and one short planning call.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working only at weekends still need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit regardless of which days the lessons fall on. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with caution.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher tutor them at the weekend?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi this is specifically ruled out. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, as this was press-reported rather than read from the source. Beyond the rules there is a practical objection: the person who sets and marks your child's school assessments should not also be paid to prepare them for those assessments.

faqs.question: Our school answers to ADEK rather than KHDA. Does that change the weekend plan?
faqs.answer: It changes two things. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and its ethics rules mean the weekend tutor comes from outside your child's school by design. It also changes supply: Abu Dhabi and particularly Al Ain have fewer IB World Schools than Dubai, so Higher Level specialists in Physics, Chemistry and Maths AA are thinner locally and weekend slots go earlier in the year. The mandatory-subject detail published by KHDA applies to Dubai schools, so check your own school's arrangements for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies directly.

faqs.question: Which IB subjects do UAE families book weekend help for most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Chemistry HL, Physics HL and Economics HL account for the bulk of weekend requests, and those are also the slots that disappear first each September. The pattern is not random: all four have either a third paper, a demanding Internal Assessment, or both, and all four reward the kind of long timed practice a weekend block allows and a weekday evening does not. English A oral rehearsal and Extended Essay process coaching are the two core requests that rise sharply between November and February, when internal deadlines land.

faqs.question: The entry deadline falls months before the papers. What should the weekend before it look like?
faqs.answer: Spent checking, not teaching. The published Pearson window shows the lead time plainly: the International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and an entry for a November sitting is settled over the preceding summer, so the list is fixed long before anyone opens a paper. Cambridge behaves the same way around its June series, with entries closing in the spring term and the exact day reaching you on the centre's statement of entry rather than from any public page. Use that weekend to read the subject list with your child, confirm each syllabus code and tier in writing with the school, and check which of Cambridge's six administrative zones your centre sits in, since Cambridge is explicit that the correct zone timetable must be used and will not take responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one. Open the board's own timetable page rather than relying on any summary, including this one.

faqs.question: My son is in DP1 and the weekend is his only free time. Will tutoring take it away?
faqs.answer: Only if it is badly arranged. One protected two-hour block on Saturday morning leaves Saturday afternoon and all of Sunday intact, which is more free time than three scattered weekday evenings leave, since each of those consumes a whole evening around it. The genuine risk is scope creep: a second subject added in October, a third in January, and by February the weekend is gone. The half-term review exists for that. If the gap has closed, the honest recommendation is to stop, and a tutor who never recommends stopping is selling hours.

faqs.question: Does a weekend tutor cover Arabic and Islamic Education alongside the IB subjects?
faqs.answer: They can, and in Dubai it is more often needed than families expect. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the grade frequently holds a report back while everyone is watching the IB subjects. One constraint matters: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so support works from your child's own school material rather than from a parallel syllabus. KHDA also organises these classes separately for Arabs and non-Arabs.

faqs.question: If there is no weekend slot left with a Chemistry HL specialist, what happens then?
faqs.answer: You get told that, which is not what happens elsewhere in this market. There are four honest responses and we will put them to you: wait for a slot and run midweek meanwhile, take Sunday or Friday evening instead, take a shorter weekly block with the specialist rather than a longer one with a generalist, or take a tutor outside UAE hours whose availability maps onto a Gulf Standard Time weekend morning. The pool includes UAE-based specialists and specialists elsewhere, including India, and you will know where your child's tutor is teaching from before the first lesson rather than after it.

weekend-ib-tutor.closingHeading: Book one Saturday and judge what comes back
weekend-ib-tutor.closingBody: The cheapest way to test everything on this page is a single weekend lesson. It costs nothing, needs no card details, runs in the slot you intend to keep with the tutor you would keep, and uses a topic from your child's current school work rather than a prepared demonstration. Afterwards you get a written note and a one-page plan counted backwards from the exam window. Judge those two documents. If the note names a topic, the marks lost and a task for the week, you have found a weekend IB tutor worth the hour. If it says the session went well, keep looking, and tell us why so the next match is better.
